# PSCAD-Compatible Electromagnetic Transients (`.pscx`, `.pslx`, `.pswx`, `.psmx`, `.psout`, `.cfg`, `.dat`)

The `@modelscript/pscad` language plugin (`languages/pscad`) provides native support for **PSCAD-compatible** projects, multi-project workspaces, component libraries, and **IEEE C37.111 COMTRADE** transient waveform recordings. It integrates directly with ModelScript's polyglot `WorkspaceIndex`, the **Dommel Companion-Circuit EMT Solver** (`@modelscript/simulate`), and the **Triple Graph Grammar (TGG)** synchronization engine.

---

## Supported File Formats

| Extension | Format                        | Description                                                                                                           |
| :-------- | :---------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.pscx`   | PSCAD Case XML                | Schematic canvas, wire segments, bus nodes, RLC/transformer/converter components, T-lines, and EMT runtime settings   |
| `.pslx`   | PSCAD Library XML             | Custom user-defined component definitions, port graphics, parameter forms, and embedded FORTRAN/EMTDC script sections |
| `.pswx`   | PSCAD Workspace XML           | Multi-project workspace manifest indexing `.pscx` cases and `.pslx` libraries via `PscadWorkspaceIndex`               |
| `.psmx`   | PSCAD Consolidated Module XML | Consolidated simulation module metadata, hierarchy mappings, and build outputs                                        |
| `.psout`  | PSCAD V5+ Binary Waveform     | Slotted-page binary waveform container with multi-run traces, channel descriptors, and fast random access             |
| `.cfg`    | IEEE C37.111 Configuration    | COMTRADE station metadata, analog/digital channel definitions, primary/secondary scaling factors, and sampling rates  |
| `.dat`    | IEEE C37.111 Data             | ASCII or 16/32-bit Binary transient waveform time-series samples                                                      |

---

## Architecture & Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Input["PSCAD & COMTRADE Artifacts"]
        PSCX[".pscx / .pslx / .pswx / .psmx"]
        COM[".cfg + .dat (COMTRADE)"]
    end

    subgraph Parser["@modelscript/pscad"]
        GLR["WASM GLR XML Parser"]
        EXT["Schematic & Netlist Extractor"]
        LINT["EMT Semantic Linter (PSCAD001–007)"]
    end

    subgraph Runtime["Compilation & Co-Simulation"]
        PROJ_MO["Modelica Projection (.mo)"]
        PROJ_SSD["SSP Topology Projection (.ssd)"]
        DOMMEL["Dommel Nodal EMT Solver (G·v = i_hist)"]
        BERGERON["Bergeron Traveling-Wave Lines"]
    end

    PSCX --> GLR --> EXT --> LINT
    EXT --> PROJ_MO
    EXT --> PROJ_SSD
    EXT --> DOMMEL
    DOMMEL <--> BERGERON
    COM --> DOMMEL
```

---

## 1. Schematic & Netlist Extraction (`emt-netlist.ts`, `pscx-parser.ts`)

PSCAD `.pscx` files represent schematics visually using a 2D coordinate grid (`User` component instances and orthogonal `Wire` segments) rather than an explicit netlist. `@modelscript/pscad` reconstructs the electrical topology deterministically:

1. **Local `master.pslx` Dynamic Ingestion**: Automatically discovers user-provided licensed `master.pslx` files via `PSCAD_MASTER_LIB_PATH` or workspace roots (`master.pslx`, `.pscad/master.pslx`, `.cache/pscad-corpus/`). When present, component definitions, multi-tab parameter forms, port configurations, and FlyBy documentation are dynamically synthesized into LSP catalogs and UI palettes with zero manual authoring.
2. **Topological Wire Snapping & Junction Synthesis**: Performs geometric point-on-segment intersection across all orthogonal `<Wire>` segments and component pin coordinates. Synthesizes topological junction nodes (`junc_${x}_${y}`) at wire-to-wire T-junctions and crossings, eliminating unattached dangling edges and reaching over 94% wire attachment on complex multi-layer industrial benchmarks.
3. **100% Component Lowering Coverage**: Lowers schematic graphs into a structured `EmtNetlist` with 100% component lowering coverage across industrial benchmarks (e.g. `DC_EMT_compare.pscx` with 1433/1433 lowered components and `DC_EMT_demo.pscx` with 597/597 lowered components):
   - AC/DC Thévenin sources, battery energy storage systems (`battery`), controlled current sources (`src_ccin_1`)
   - 6th-order synchronous machines, 5th-order induction/DFIG wind machines, and wound-rotor induction machines (`wound_rotor`)
   - Distributed-parameter Bergeron traveling-wave lines, lumped $\pi$-sections, and multi-conductor cables
   - Non-linear MOV surge arresters, VSC PWM converters, 6-pulse thyristor bridges, and MMC converter stations
   - 20+ CSMF control transfer-function blocks (`const`, `gain`, `pi_ctlr`, `realpole`, `leadlag`, `limit`, `sum`, `rms3ph`, `abcdq0`) and black-box vendor IBR FMUs.
4. **Workspace Indexing (`PscadWorkspaceIndex`)**: Resolves cross-file references across `.pswx` workspaces, linking custom `<Definition>` blocks in `.pslx` libraries to `<User>` instances in `.pscx` cases.

---

## 2. Pre-Flight Electrical Lint Rules

`@modelscript/pscad` enforces 17 electromagnetic transient modeling best practices before simulation starts, providing 1-click LSP Quick-Fix actions:

### Diagnostics for PSCAD / EMTDC (55 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M6001` | error | `floating-electrical-node` | Electrical node '<nodeName>' is floating with no closed connections. |
| `M6002` | warning | `transformer-winding-mismatch` | Transformer '<xfmrName>' <side> rating (<ratedKv> kV) does not match connected bus base (<busKv> kV). |
| `M6003` | error | `invalid-parameter-bounds` | Component '<elemName>' parameter '<paramName>' = <val> is invalid: <reason>. |
| `M6004` | warning | `weak-grid-warning` | Point of Interconnection '<poiBus>' has low Short-Circuit Ratio (SCR = <value> < 1.5). IBR control stability risks detected. |
| `M6005` | error | `csmf-unresolved-input` | CSMF control block '<blockId>' references unresolved upstream signal block '<missingInputId>'. |
| `M6006` | error | `line-travel-time-underflow` | Transmission line '<lineId>' wave propagation delay (<value> us) is smaller than simulation time step (<value> us). Reduce time step or use a lumped pi-section model. |
| `M6007` | error | `sync-machine-reactance-order` | Synchronous machine '<machineId>' violates physical d-axis reactance hierarchy (Xd=<xd> >= Xd'=<xdPrime> >= Xd''=<xdSub> pu required). |
| `M6008` | warning | `mov-arrester-under-rated` | MOV surge arrester '<arresterId>' reference voltage (<value> kV) is below connected bus '<busName>' nominal phase-to-ground peak voltage (<value> kV), causing continuous thermal conduction. |
| `M6009` | error | `duplicate-component-id` | Duplicate component or bus ID '<id>' declared in schematic module '<modName>'. |
| `M6010` | error | `bus-voltage-conflict` | Conductive net shorts bus '<busA>' (<kvA> kV) directly to bus '<busB>' (<kvB> kV) without an intervening transformer. |
| `M6011` | error | `port-domain-mismatch` | Wire '<wireId>' connects control signal port '<sigPort>' directly to 3-phase electrical port '<elecPort>'. |
| `M6012` | error | `csmf-algebraic-loop` | CSMF control blocks form an algebraic loop with no state or delay element: <cycle>. |
| `M6013` | error | `parallel-ideal-sources` | Ideal voltage sources <sourceIds> are connected in parallel at bus '<busName>', making the nodal matrix singular. |
| `M6014` | warning | `parallel-low-impedance-sources` | Voltage sources <sourceIds> are connected in parallel at bus '<busName>' with no declared source impedance; a stiff default impedance is assumed and large circulating currents may result. |
| `M6015` | warning | `limiter-permanently-saturated` | Limiter '<blockId>' is permanently saturated: its input stays within [<inLo>, <inHi>] but its output limits are [<limLo>, <limHi>]. |
| `M6016` | error | `component-check-failed` | Component '<cmpName>' check failed: <reason>. |
| `M6017` | warning | `component-check-warning` | Component '<cmpName>' check warning: <reason>. |
| `M6021` | warning | `unresolved-component-definition` | Component '<cmpName>' references definition '<defName>', which is not found in the project or loaded .pslx libraries. |
| `M6022` | warning | `wire-near-miss` | Wire '<wireId>' endpoint is <value> px from '<targetName>' (outside snap tolerance 15 px), leaving an unintentional open circuit. |
| `M6023` | warning | `overlapping-wire-segments` | Wire '<wireA>' overlaps collinearly with wire '<wireB>'; verify whether a junction or unintentional short exists. |
| `M6024` | warning | `dangling-wireless-signal` | Wireless signal tag '<tagName>' (<kind>) is dangling: <reason>. |
| `M6025` | error | `vector-signal-dimension-mismatch` | Signal vector dimension mismatch: '<srcPort>' (dim=<srcDim>) cannot connect directly to '<dstPort>' (dim=<dstDim>). |
| `M6026` | error | `phase-dimension-mismatch` | Wire '<wireId>' connects 3-phase port '<port3p>' directly to 1-phase port '<port1p>' without a breakout block. |
| `M6027` | error | `submodule-port-interface-mismatch` | Submodule instance '<cmpName>' (<defName>) port interface mismatch: <detail>. |
| `M6028` | info | `unlowered-simulatable-component` | Component '<cmpName>' (<defName>) is not lowered into the native EMT netlist and will be omitted from standalone simulation. |
| `M6029` | error | `parameter-expression-eval-error` | Component '<cmpName>' parameter '<paramKey>' expression '<rawExpr>' failed to evaluate to a finite value. |
| `M6030` | warning | `pgb-output-channel-duplicate-or-unwired` | Output channel (pgb) '<channelName>' <reason>. |
| `M6031` | warning | `system-frequency-mismatch` | Element '<elemName>' is rated at <elemFreqHz> Hz, which differs from the project system frequency (<sysFreqHz> Hz). |
| `M6032` | warning | `rms-vs-peak-voltage-entry-suspect` | Source '<srcName>' voltage (<enteredKv> kV) differs from connected bus '<busName>' (<busKv> kV L-L RMS) by <hint>. |
| `M6040` | warning | `pwm-step-nyquist-violation` | PWM/switching block '<cmpName>' operates at <carrierHz> Hz while EMT time step \\u0394t=<dtUs> us yields <10 steps/cycle (recommend \\u0394t <= <value> us). |
| `M6041` | warning | `control-time-constant-underflow` | CSMF control block '<blockId>' has time constant <value> us < 2*\\u0394t (<value> us), causing numerical aliasing/instability. |
| `M6042` | warning | `plot-step-aliasing-hazard` | Plot sampling step (<plotStepUs> us > 10*\\u0394t where \\u0394t=<dtUs> us) lowers Nyquist frequency to <value> Hz and risks aliasing switching harmonics. |
| `M6043` | error | `cutset-of-inductors-and-current-sources` | Inductive/current-source cutset at bus '<busId>' for '<elemId>' has no parallel resistive/snubber path (causes DAE index-2 di/dt impulse). |
| `M6044` | error | `loop-of-capacitors-and-voltage-sources` | Zero-impedance closed loop detected across switches/jumpers (<cycleDesc>), making the Dommel nodal matrix singular. |
| `M6045` | warning | `missing-switch-snubber-chatter-risk` | Switching device '<elemName>' (<defName>) has no RC snubber parameters while CDA chatter elimination is disabled. |
| `M6046` | warning | `nodal-conductance-matrix-ill-conditioned` | Dommel nodal conductance ratio Gmax/Gmin = <value> (<value> S / <value> S) exceeds 1e11 and risks IEEE-754 mantissa loss. |
| `M6047` | error | `ulm-vector-fitting-passivity-violation` | Transmission line '<lineId>' rational vector fit violates passivity: <detail>. |
| `M6048` | error | `transformer-magnetizing-inrush-remanence-invalid` | Saturable transformer '<xfmrId>' magnetizing/remanence configuration is invalid: <detail>. |
| `M6049` | warning | `subsynchronous-series-resonance-risk` | Series capacitor '<capId>' in series with inductive element '<indId>' resonates at <value> Hz (< <fBaseHz> Hz nominal), creating subsynchronous resonance (SSR/SSCI) risk. |
| `M6060` | info | `csmf-dead-limiter-never-activates` | Limiter '<blockId>' never saturates: input interval [<inLo>, <inHi>] stays strictly inside limits [<limLo>, <limHi>]. |
| `M6061` | error | `csmf-domain-hazard` | CSMF block '<blockId>' (<kind>) has a mathematical domain hazard: <reason>. |
| `M6062` | warning | `pi-integrator-unbounded` | CSMF '<kind>' block '<blockId>' has unbounded output limits and may wind up indefinitely under saturation. |
| `M6063` | info | `csmf-relational-cancelation-zonotope` | Zonotope analysis tightened correlated control block '<blockId>' from [<value>, <value>] to [<value>, <value>]. |
| `M6064` | warning | `pll-bandwidth-weak-grid-instability` | PLL '<pllName>' high bandwidth (<value> Hz > 25 Hz) coupled to weak grid (SCR = <value> < 2.0) risks synchronization instability. |
| `M6065` | error | `fortran-udm-hazard` | Definition '<defName>' Fortran segment '<segmentName>' hazard: <reason>. |
| `M6066` | warning | `fortran-udm-uninitialized-history-state` | Definition '<defName>' segment '<segName>' reads '<arrayName>' before any prior store or TIMEZERO initialization guard. |
| `M6067` | error | `fortran-udm-non-reentrant-global-common` | Definition '<defName>' uses a shared Fortran COMMON block while instantiated <instances> times in the project (causes cross-instance state corruption; use STORF/STORI instead). |
| `M6068` | warning | `oem-dll-abi-and-license-preflight` | OEM black-box DLL block '<cmpName>' pre-flight warning: <detail>. |

---

## 3. IEEE 2800-2022 & NERC PRC-029-1 Grid-Code Verification

`@modelscript/pscad` includes an automated verification engine for Inverter-Based Resource (IBR) grid interconnection standards (`verifyIeee2800Compliance`):

- **Phasor & Sequence Extraction**: Sliding 1-cycle fundamental DFT computes symmetrical components ($V_0, V_1, V_2, I_0, I_1, I_2$) and synchronous $dq$-frame currents ($I_{1d}, I_{1q}$).
- **Mandatory Clauses**:
  - **Clause 5.3.2 / 7.2.2.3**: Low/High Voltage Ride-Through (LVRT/HVRT) and Prohibition of Momentary Cessation.
  - **Clause 5.4.1 / 7.2.2.3.5**: Fast Dynamic Reactive Current Response ($T_{90\%} \le 50\text{ ms}$).
  - **Clause 5.4.2 / 7.2.2.1**: Post-Fault Transient Overvoltage Ceiling ($V_{\text{peak}} \le 1.20\text{ pu}$).
  - **Clause 7.2.2.1 / NERC PRC-029-1**: Piecewise Time-Voltage Ride-Through Envelope.
  - **Clause 7.2.2.3.4**: Incremental Positive & Negative-Sequence Reactive Current Droop ($k_1, k_2$).
  - **Clause 7.2.2.3.5**: Post-Fault Active Power Recovery ($\ge 90\%$ within $1.0\text{ s}$).
  - **Clause 7.3.2**: Frequency, RoCoF ($\ge 5\text{ Hz/s}$), and Instantaneous Phase-Angle Jump ($\ge 25^\circ$) Ride-Through.

---

## 4. Polyglot Projections & 15 TGG Synchronization Rules

### Modelica & SSP Projections (`projections/modelica.ts`, `projections/ssp.ts`)

- **`pscadToModelica(doc)`**: Projects a `.pscx` schematic and its reconstructed electrical nodes into standard Modelica models using `Modelica.Electrical.Analog` (`Resistor`, `Inductor`, `Capacitor`, `IdealTransformer`, `SineVoltage`, `OLine`) and `Modelica.Blocks`.
- **`pscadToSsd(doc)`**: Projects multi-subsystem PSCAD networks and T-line decoupled partitions into an **SSP 1.0 `.ssd`** System Structure Description XML document for FMI Co-Simulation.

### Bidirectional TGG Rules

15 bidirectional **Triple Graph Grammar (TGG)** rules synchronize PSCAD models with Modelica and SysML v2:
`PscadProjectToModelicaModel`, `PscadResistorToModelicaResistor`, `PscadInductorToModelicaInductor`, `PscadCapacitorToModelicaCapacitor`, `PscadTLineToModelicaOLine`, `PscadMachineToModelicaMachine`, `PscadConverterToModelicaConverter`, `PscadCsmfToModelicaBlock`, and `PscadComponentToSysmlPart`.

---

## 5. Dommel Companion EMT Solver (`@modelscript/simulate`)

For high-frequency power electronics and transient studies, `@modelscript/simulate` provides a high-performance **Electromagnetic Transient (EMT)** companion solver (`EmtSolver` in `packages/simulate/src/solvers/emt/emt-solver.ts`):

- **Dommel Trapezoidal Companion Models**: Discretizes inductors ($G_L = \frac{\Delta t}{2L}$) and capacitors ($G_C = \frac{2C}{\Delta t}$) into constant nodal conductance matrices $\mathbf{G}\mathbf{v}(t) = \mathbf{i}_{\text{hist}}(t - \Delta t) + \mathbf{i}_{\text{src}}(t)$.
- **Critical Damping Adjustment (CDA)**: Automatically switches from Trapezoidal to Backward Euler for one half-step following any breaker or power-electronic switching event to eliminate artificial numerical chatter.
- **Bergeron Traveling-Wave Lines**: Decouples sub-networks separated by transmission lines of delay $\tau \ge \Delta t$, enabling parallel sub-grid nodal solves.
- **Grounded Simulation Honesty**: Connects passive buses with realistic high-impedance ground conductances ($G = 10^{-5}\text{ S}$) without injecting artificial 230 kV reference sources, ensuring true physical fidelity.

---

## 6. IEEE C37.111 COMTRADE Reader & Writer (`comtrade.ts`)

Zero-dependency parser and serializer for IEEE Std C37.111-1999 / 2013 **COMTRADE** files (`.cfg`, `.dat`, `.cff`):

```ts
import { parseComtrade, writeComtrade, EmtSolver } from "@modelscript/pscad";

// Export an EMT simulation directly to IEEE C37.111 (.cfg + .dat)
const { cfg, dat } = writeComtrade({
  stationName: "SUB_230KV",
  recDevId: "MODELSCRIPT_EMT",
  lineFrequency: 60,
  timeTimestamps: result.time,
  analogChannels: [
    { id: "VA_BUS1", unit: "V", values: result.nodeVoltages.get(1)! },
    { id: "IA_LINE1", unit: "A", values: result.branchCurrents.get("BRK1")! },
  ],
});
```

## 7. PSCAD V5+ Binary Waveform Container (`.psout`)

PSCAD V5+ replaces legacy ASCII `.out` files with `.psout`, a high-performance slotted-page binary container format. ModelScript provides complete, zero-dependency read and write support for `.psout` across the CLI, Studio, and TypeScript APIs via an in-WASM AssemblyScript codec.

### Slotted-Page Binary Architecture

A `.psout` file is organized into 1024-byte pages:

- **Page 0 (Header)**: Magic version (`0x00010001`), total page count, page size, 128-bit project GUID, creation timestamp, and floating-point verification constants (`-1.0e-30`, `1.0e30`, `1.0e-30`).
- **Page 1 (Run Map)**: Array mapping simulation run indices to their root Call pages.
- **Page 2 (Call Map)**: Links simulation calls to their variable lists and trace descriptors.
- **Pages 3+ (String Table & Trace Descriptors)**: Null-terminated string pool for channel identifiers, units, group names, and trace metadata.
- **Trace Pages**: Slotted 64-bit IEEE 754 floating-point sample pages with forward/backward linked page lists for $O(1)$ sequential streaming and fast random seeking.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    H["Page 0: Header & GUID"] --> RM["Page 1: Run Map"]
    RM --> CM["Page 2: Call Map"]
    CM --> ST["Pages 3+: String Table & Trace Map"]
    ST --> TD["Trace Descriptors (Name, Unit, Min, Max)"]
    TD --> DATA["1024-Byte Data Pages (Float64 Vectors)"]
```

### Programmatic TypeScript API

```ts
import { readPscadPsout, writePscadPsout } from "@modelscript/pscad";

// 1. Reading and inspecting a .psout file
const bytes = new Uint8Array(fs.readFileSync("Cigre.psout"));
const doc = readPscadPsout(bytes);

console.log(`Version: ${doc.header.version}, Pages: ${doc.header.pageCount}`);
console.log(`Created: ${doc.header.createdOn.toISOString()}`);

// Access traces and convert to standard SimulationResult
const run0 = doc.run(0);
for (const [id, trace] of run0.traces) {
  console.log(`Channel ${id}: ${trace.name} [${trace.unit}] (${trace.values.length} samples)`);
}

const simResult = doc.toSimulationResult(0);
console.log(`Time vector length: ${simResult.time.length}`);

// 2. Writing simulation results to .psout
const outBytes = await writePscadPsout(simResult, {
  projectName: "IEEE_39_Bus",
  version: 1,
});
fs.writeFileSync("output.psout", outBytes);
```

### Command-Line Interface (`msx pscad`)

#### 1. Inspection, Linting, Schematic Diff & IEEE 2800 Verification

```bash
# Inspect project components, wire nets, and pre-flight lint rules (M6001-M6017)
msx pscad inspect models/benchmark.pscx
msx pscad lint models/benchmark.pscx

# Render schematic diagram SVG or compute visual schematic diff between two revisions
msx pscad diagram models/benchmark.pscx --out=schematic.svg
msx pscad diff models/rev1.pscx models/rev2.pscx

# Verify IEEE 2800-2022 & NERC PRC-029-1 fault ride-through compliance
msx pscad verify-ieee2800 models/benchmark.pscx

# Project to Modelica or System Structure & Parameterization (SSP)
msx pscad to-modelica models/benchmark.pscx --out=Benchmark.mo
msx pscad to-ssp models/benchmark.pscx --out=SystemStructure.ssd
```

#### 2. Simulation Export to `.psout` & COMTRADE Conversion

```bash
# Simulate a PSCAD case and export directly to .psout
msx pscad sim models/benchmark.pscx --format=psout --out=results.psout

# Print formatted ANSI metadata table and channel telemetry
msx pscad psout results.psout

# Convert .psout to CSV or IEEE C37.111 COMTRADE (.cfg + .dat)
msx pscad psout results.psout --out=telemetry.csv
msx pscad psout results.psout --format=comtrade
```

### Studio & VS Code Waveform Viewer (`modelscript.psoutViewer`)

When opening any `*.psout` file in Studio or VS Code, the custom editor provides a dark-mode waveform analysis viewport:

1. **Multi-Channel Canvas Chart**: High-performance 60 FPS HTML5 canvas rendering with LTTB (Largest-Triangle-Three-Buckets) decimation for multi-million-sample transients.
2. **Dual Measurement Cursors**: Live measurement HUD calculating time difference ($\Delta t$), instantaneous frequency ($f = 1/\Delta t$), amplitude change ($\Delta y$), and rate-of-change ($\text{dy/dt}$ slope).
3. **Channel Palette**: Real-time signal search filter, group filtering, color chips, and visibility toggles.
4. **Quick Export**: One-click toolbar actions to export displayed channels to CSV or IEEE C37.111 COMTRADE.

# PSS/E-Compatible Transmission Power Flow (`.raw`)

The `@modelscript/psse` language package (`languages/psse`) provides native support for **PSS/E-compatible RAW (`.raw`)** transmission grid power flow base cases (Revisions 30 through 35). It delivers streaming parsing, round-trip serialization, pre-flight topological linting (`P1001`–`P4001`), sparse nodal admittance matrix ($Y_{bus} = G + jB$) assembly, in-engine non-linear AC power flow solving (Newton-Raphson & Fast Decoupled), multi-domain projections to **Modelica** and **PSCAD/EMT**, interactive Single-Line Diagrams (SLD) via AntV X6, and a dual-mode VS Code custom webview editor.

---

## Supported File Specifications

| Revision     | Specification        | Key Structural Features                                                                          |
| :----------- | :------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **PSS/E-30** | Legacy Planning Deck | 6-character bus names, integer area/zone codes, fixed branch thermal rating blocks               |
| **PSS/E-32** | Extended Format      | 12-character alphanumeric bus names, expanded DC line modeling, switched shunt blocks            |
| **PSS/E-33** | Modern Standard      | Canonical 12-character names, multi-section lines, 2-terminal & VSC DC transmission, GIC records |
| **PSS/E-34** | Substation-Oriented  | Node-breaker topologies, explicit substation IDs, multi-terminal DC grids                        |
| **PSS/E-35** | High-Density Matrix  | Extended branch identifiers, expanded transformer winding data, flexible rating vectors          |

---

## Architecture & Compilation Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    RAW["PSS/E RAW Base Case (.raw)"]

    subgraph FrontEnd["Parser & Static Analysis"]
        WASM["Native WebAssembly GLR Parser"]
        STREAM["Streaming Robust Fallback Parser"]
        INDEX["PsseWorkspaceIndex (Salsa Memoization)"]
        LINT["Pre-flight Topology Linter (P1001–P4002)"]
    end

    subgraph Core["Analytical & Numerical Solvers"]
        YBUS["Sparse Admittance Matrix (Ybus = G + jB)"]
        SOLVER["Non-Linear AC Power Flow (NR & FDPF)"]
        METRICS["Losses, Violations & Thermal Loading"]
    end

    subgraph Projections["Multi-Domain Projections"]
        MO["Modelica Acausal Model (psseToModelica)"]
        EMT["PSCAD / EMT Netlist (psseToEmtNetlist)"]
    end

    subgraph Presentation["User Experience & Toolchain"]
        SLD["AntV X6 & SVG Single-Line Diagram"]
        IDE["Dual-Mode Visual Custom Editor"]
        CLI["CLI Toolchain (msx psse)"]
    end

    RAW --> WASM & STREAM
    WASM & STREAM --> INDEX --> LINT
    INDEX --> YBUS --> SOLVER --> METRICS
    INDEX --> MO & EMT
    METRICS & YBUS --> SLD & IDE & CLI
```

| `P8001` | error | `ras-sps-chattering-or-race-condition` | Formal BMC/SAT check proved contradictory RAS/SPS race on '<target>': '<schemeA>' and '<schemeB>' can trigger opposing actions simultaneously. |

| `P8019` | info | `formal-proof-manifest-summary` | Formal verification proof manifest generated (<passed>/<total> obligations certified, digest=<digest>). |

---

## 2. Sparse Nodal Admittance Matrix ($Y_{bus}$)

The network admittance matrix $\mathbf{Y}_{\text{bus}} \in \mathbb{C}^{N \times N}$ is extracted via `extractPowerFlowNetlist()` in `languages/psse/src/netlist/powerflow-netlist.ts`:

### Transmission Lines ($\pi$-Equivalent)

For a branch connecting buses $i$ and $j$ with series impedance $z = r + jx$ and total line charging susceptance $b$, the series admittance $y_s$ is stamped into the off-diagonal mutual entries ($Y_{ij}, Y_{ji}$) with a negative sign and added—along with half the line charging susceptance $j\frac{b}{2}$—to each terminal bus's self-admittance ($Y_{ii}, Y_{jj}$):

$$y_s = \frac{1}{r + jx} = \frac{r - jx}{r^2 + x^2} = g_s + j b_s$$
$$Y_{ij} = -y_s,\quad Y_{ji} = -y_s$$
$$Y_{ii} \mathrel{+}= y_s + j\frac{b}{2},\quad Y_{jj} \mathrel{+}= y_s + j\frac{b}{2}$$

### Transformers with Complex Tap Ratio

For a transformer with off-nominal turns ratio magnitude $a$ and phase-shift angle $\phi$, the complex tap $\bar{a} = a e^{j\phi} = a_{\text{re}} + j a_{\text{im}}$ scales the primary-side self-admittance by $|\bar{a}|^{-2}$ and introduces conjugate-asymmetric mutual couplings between the primary ($i$) and secondary ($j$) buses:

$$Y_{ii} \mathrel{+}= \frac{y_s}{|\bar{a}|^2},\quad Y_{jj} \mathrel{+}= y_s$$
$$Y_{ij} = -\frac{y_s}{\bar{a}^*},\quad Y_{ji} = -\frac{y_s}{\bar{a}}$$

| Symbol                           | Meaning                                                                     | Units / Domain                |
| :------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------- |
| $y_s, g_s, b_s$                  | Series branch admittance, conductance, and susceptance                      | $\text{p.u.}$ (or $\text{S}$) |
| $r, x$                           | Series branch resistance and reactance                                      | $\text{p.u.}$ (or $\Omega$)   |
| $b$                              | Total line shunt charging susceptance                                       | $\text{p.u.}$ (or $\text{S}$) |
| $j$                              | Imaginary unit ($\sqrt{-1}$)                                                | Dimensionless                 |
| $Y_{ii}, Y_{jj}, Y_{ij}, Y_{ji}$ | Self and mutual entries of $\mathbf{Y}_{\text{bus}}$                        | $\text{p.u.}$ (or $\text{S}$) |
| $\bar{a}, \bar{a}^*$             | Complex off-nominal transformer tap ratio ($a e^{j\phi}$) and its conjugate | Dimensionless                 |

---

## 3. In-Engine Non-Linear AC Power Flow Solver

`@modelscript/psse` includes an exact, non-linear AC Power Flow engine (`solvePowerFlow()` in `languages/psse/src/solver/ac-powerflow.ts`) supporting both **Newton-Raphson** and **Fast Decoupled Power Flow (FDPF)**:

### Mismatch Formulation

For each bus $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ with voltage phasor $\bar{V}_i = V_i e^{j\theta_i}$, the calculated net active ($P_i$) and reactive ($Q_i$) power injections sum the power flowing into all connected buses, and the mismatches ($\Delta P_i, \Delta Q_i$) measure the residual difference from the scheduled generator/load injections:

$$P_i(V, \theta) = V_i \sum_{k=1}^N V_k \left( G_{ik} \cos\theta_{ik} + B_{ik} \sin\theta_{ik} \right)$$
$$Q_i(V, \theta) = V_i \sum_{k=1}^N V_k \left( G_{ik} \sin\theta_{ik} - B_{ik} \cos\theta_{ik} \right)$$
where $\theta_{ik} = \theta_i - \theta_k$. Active and reactive mismatches are:
$$\Delta P_i = P_i^{\text{spec}} - P_i(V, \theta),\quad \Delta Q_i = Q_i^{\text{spec}} - Q_i(V, \theta)$$

### Analytical Jacobian & Adaptive Damping

At each Newton-Raphson iteration, the non-linear mismatch equations are linearized around the current voltage state to solve for the phase-angle ($\Delta \theta$) and normalized voltage-magnitude ($\Delta V / V$) updates:

$$\begin{bmatrix} \Delta P \\ \Delta Q \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} H & N \\ M & L \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \Delta \theta \\ \Delta V / V \end{bmatrix}$$

| Symbol                                          | Meaning                                                                                                                                                             | Units / Domain    |
| :---------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :---------------- |
| $N$                                             | Total number of buses in the network                                                                                                                                | Integer ($\ge 1$) |
| $V_i, V_k, \Delta V$                            | Bus voltage magnitudes and voltage update vector                                                                                                                    | $\text{p.u.}$     |
| $\theta_i, \theta_k, \theta_{ik}, \Delta\theta$ | Bus voltage phase angles, angle difference ($\theta_i - \theta_k$), and angle update vector                                                                         | $\text{rad}$      |
| $G_{ik}, B_{ik}$                                | Real (conductance) and imaginary (susceptance) parts of $Y_{ik}$                                                                                                    | $\text{p.u.}$     |
| $P_i, Q_i$                                      | Calculated net active and reactive power injections at bus $i$                                                                                                      | $\text{p.u.}$     |
| $P_i^{\text{spec}}, Q_i^{\text{spec}}$          | Specified net active and reactive power injections at bus $i$                                                                                                       | $\text{p.u.}$     |
| $\Delta P_i, \Delta Q_i, \Delta P, \Delta Q$    | Active and reactive power mismatch scalars and vectors                                                                                                              | $\text{p.u.}$     |
| $H, N, M, L$                                    | Jacobian block submatrices ($\frac{\partial P}{\partial\theta}, V\frac{\partial P}{\partial V}, \frac{\partial Q}{\partial\theta}, V\frac{\partial Q}{\partial V}$) | $\text{p.u.}$     |

- **$H\_{ik} = \frac{\partial P_i}{\partial \theta_k} = V_i V_k (G\_{ik} \sin\theta\_{ik} - B\_{ik} \cos\theta\_{ik})$** ($k \ne i$), and $H_{ii} = -Q_i - B_{ii} V_i^2$.
- **$N\_{ik} = V_k \frac{\partial P_i}{\partial V_k} = V_i V_k (G\_{ik} \cos\theta\_{ik} + B\_{ik} \sin\theta\_{ik})$** ($k \ne i$), and $N_{ii} = P_i + G_{ii} V_i^2$.
- **$M\_{ik} = \frac{\partial Q_i}{\partial \theta_k} = -V_i V_k (G\_{ik} \cos\theta\_{ik} + B\_{ik} \sin\theta\_{ik})$** ($k \ne i$), and $M_{ii} = P_i - G_{ii} V_i^2$.
- **$L\_{ik} = V_k \frac{\partial Q_i}{\partial V_k} = V_i V_k (G\_{ik} \sin\theta\_{ik} - B\_{ik} \cos\theta\_{ik})$** ($k \ne i$), and $L_{ii} = Q_i - B_{ii} V_i^2$.

### Generator $Q$-Limit Clamping & PV-to-PQ Switching

When $Q_g > Q_{\max}$ or $Q_g < Q_{\min}$, the generator bus is clamped at its reactive limit and dynamically converted to a PQ bus for remaining iterations, preventing unrealistic voltage regulation.

---

## 4. Multi-Domain Interoperability Projections

### Projection to Modelica (`psseToModelica`)

Projects a `.raw` case into a clean, strongly-typed Modelica physical system model:

- **Buses** mapped to equipotential AC pins.
- **Generators** mapped to sinusoidal voltage sources (`Modelica.Electrical.Analog.Sources.SineVoltage`).
- **Branches** mapped to series R-L models (`Modelica.Electrical.Analog.Basic.Resistor` + `Inductor`).
- **Loads** mapped to constant active and reactive impedance networks.

```modelica
model Ieee14Test
  Modelica.Electrical.Analog.Basic.Ground ground;
  Modelica.Electrical.Analog.Sources.SineVoltage gen_1_1(V = 106.0, f = 60.0);
  Modelica.Electrical.Analog.Basic.Resistor line_1_2_r(R = 0.01938);
  Modelica.Electrical.Analog.Basic.Inductor line_1_2_l(L = 0.0001569);
equation
  connect(gen_1_1.n, ground.p);
  connect(gen_1_1.p, line_1_2_r.p);
  connect(line_1_2_r.n, line_1_2_l.p);
end Ieee14Test;
```

### Projection to PSCAD / EMT Netlist (`psseToEmtNetlist`)

Generates multi-bus companion-circuit netlists compatible with ModelScript's Dommel EMT solver (`@modelscript/simulate`) for transient stability and electromagnetic switching studies.

### Advanced Bulk Grid Studies: WebGPU $N-1$, OPF, Modes, PMU Calibration & NERC Auditing

- **Batched WebGPU $N-1$ Contingency Screener & ACCC Benchmarking (`n1`, `benchmark`)**: Evaluates post-contingency thermal line loadings and bus voltage excursions across single-element outages (`webgpu-contingency-screener.ts`, `accc-benchmarker.ts`).
- **Optimal Power Flow, Short-Circuit, Small-Signal Modes & Continuation Power Flow (`opf`, `fault`, `modes`, `cpf`)**: AC/DC OPF dispatch, IEC 60909 / ANSI fault current calculation, Sparse Arnoldi electromechanical modal analysis, and nose-curve voltage stability margin evaluation.
- **PMU SMIB Event Playback & `.dyr` Parameter Calibration (`pmu-calibrate`)**: Replays synchrophasor voltage and frequency trajectories into a Single-Machine Infinite-Bus (SMIB) harness (`pmu-smib-harness.ts`) and calibrates `.dyr` generator/exciter/IBR parameters (`dyr-calibrator.ts`).
- **NERC Collector Equivalencing & Protection Auditing (`collector-equiv`, `verify-nerc`, `audit-protection`)**: Aggregates radial wind/solar collector feeders into single-machine equivalents (`collector-equivalencer.ts`) and audits NERC TPL-001-5, PRC-019, PRC-024, PRC-025, and PRC-026 compliance (`protection-auditor.ts`).

## 5. Command-Line Interface (`msx psse`)

ModelScript's CLI provides headless inspection, linting, diagram rendering, power flow solving, and compliance auditing:

```bash
# Display summary of buses, generators, loads, branches, and MW totals
msx psse summary case.raw
msx psse inspect case.raw

# Run pre-flight electrical topology and bounds linter
msx psse lint case.raw

# Solve non-linear AC power flow with Newton-Raphson (default) or Fast Decoupled
msx psse solve case.raw
msx psse solve case.raw --algorithm=fdpf --tol=1e-5 --max-iter=30

# Run AC/DC Optimal Power Flow, short-circuit faults, small-signal modes, N-1 contingencies, and CPF
msx psse opf case.raw
msx psse fault case.raw
msx psse modes case.raw
msx psse n1 case.raw
msx psse cpf case.raw

# Calibrate .dyr dynamic parameters against PMU playback, aggregate collector systems, and audit NERC compliance
msx psse pmu-calibrate case.raw
msx psse collector-equiv case.raw
msx psse verify-nerc case.raw
msx psse audit-protection case.raw

# Export publication-quality Single-Line Diagram SVG, Modelica, DAE, or CGMES
msx psse diagram case.raw --out=grid.svg
msx psse to-modelica case.raw --out=grid.mo
msx psse to-dae case.raw --out=grid.dae.json
msx psse to-cgmes case.raw --out=grid.xml
msx psse netlist case.raw
```

## 6. Custom Visual Webview Editor (`modelscript.rawEditor`)

Opening any `.raw` file in the Ansatz Studio or VS Code launches the custom dual-mode editor:

- **Single-Line Diagram View**: Interactive pan/zoom SVG canvas with voltage-tier color coding (345 kV red, 138 kV blue, 69 kV green), power flow overlays, and generator/transformer glyphs.
- **High-Density Tabular Grid**: Live-filterable tables for Buses, Generators, Branches, Transformers, and Loads with search.
- **Overload & Violation Badges**: Automatic highlight of under-voltage ($V < 0.95\text{ pu}$), over-voltage ($V > 1.05\text{ pu}$), and thermal line overloads ($S_{ij} > \text{Rate A}$).
- **Export Toolbar**: Export to SVG diagrams, Modelica `.mo` packages, and PSCAD/EMT netlists.

# DIgSILENT PowerFactory-Compatible Grid Modeling (`.dz`, `.pfd`, `.dsl`)

The `@modelscript/powerfactory` language package (`languages/powerfactory`) provides native support for **DIgSILENT PowerFactory-compatible** project archives (`.dz`), database exports (`.pfd`, `.xml`), and **DIgSILENT Simulation Language (`.dsl`)** dynamic block definitions. It delivers node-breaker to bus-branch topology reduction, pre-flight electrical validation (`PF1001`–`PF1008`), AC/DC Optimal Power Flow (`solvePowerFactoryOpf`), Quasi-Dynamic Simulation (`solvePowerFactoryQdsl`), harmonic load flow, IEC 60909 short-circuit analysis, Sparse Arnoldi small-signal modal analysis, IEEE 738 Dynamic Line Rating (DLR), Single-Line Diagram (SLD) rendering (`IntGrf` / `SetDesktop`), and cross-domain projections to **PSS/E** and **Modelica (OpenIPSL)**.

---

## Supported Object Classes & File Formats

| Format / Class              | Specification                       | Key Structural Features                                                                                   |
| :-------------------------- | :---------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **`.dz` / `.pfd` / `.xml`** | Project Archive & Database Export   | Substations (`ElmSubstat`), terminals (`ElmTerm`), switches (`StaSwitch`, `ElmCoup`), graphic netboards   |
| **`ElmLne` / `TypLne`**     | AC Transmission Lines & Cables      | Positive/zero-sequence impedance ($R_1, X_1, B_1, R_0, X_0, B_0$), thermal rating, parallel circuits      |
| **`ElmTr2` / `ElmTr3`**     | 2- & 3-Winding Power Transformers   | HV/MV/LV nominal voltages, vector groups (`YNd11`, `Dyn5`), off-nominal tap changers, short-circuit $u_k$ |
| **`ElmSym` / `ElmGenstat`** | Synchronous & Static IBR Generators | Active/reactive dispatch, voltage setpoint $u_{\text{setp}}$, capability curves, synchronous reactances   |
| **`.dsl` (`BlkDef`)**       | DIgSILENT Simulation Language       | Continuous transfer functions, PI/lag/lead-lag blocks, state derivatives, and non-linear limiters         |

---

## Architecture & Compilation Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PF["PowerFactory Archive (.dz / .pfd / .xml / .dsl)"]

    subgraph FrontEnd["Ingestion & Topology Processor"]
        PARSE["Archive & XML/PFD Object Parser"]
        TOPO["Disjoint-Set Node-Breaker Topology Processor"]
        DSL["DSL Transfer-Function & Block Compiler"]
        LINT["Pre-Flight Grid Linter (PF1001–PF1008)"]
    end

    subgraph Solvers["Power System & Protection Solvers"]
        ACPF["AC Power Flow & AC/DC OPF"]
        SC["IEC 60909 Short-Circuit & Protection"]
        MODES["Sparse Arnoldi Small-Signal Eigenvalues"]
        HARM["Harmonic Load Flow & IEEE 738 DLR"]
    end

    subgraph Projections["Multi-Domain Projections"]
        PSSE["PSS/E v33 RAW & DYR (powerFactoryToPsse)"]
        MO["OpenIPSL Modelica 3.x (powerFactoryToModelica)"]
        SLD["Single-Line Diagram SVG (renderPowerFactorySvg)"]
    end

    PF --> PARSE & DSL
    PARSE --> TOPO --> LINT
    TOPO --> ACPF & SC & MODES & HARM
    TOPO & DSL --> PSSE & MO & SLD
```

## 1. Pre-Flight Electrical Diagnostic Rules

`@modelscript/powerfactory` validates terminal connectivity, line/transformer type references, and generator operating bounds prior to network reduction or simulation:

### Diagnostics for DIgSILENT PowerFactory (6 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `PF1001` | warning | `floating-terminal` | Terminal '<terminalName>' is floating and not connected to any electrical equipment. |
| `PF1002` | error | `invalid-line-parameters` | Line '<lineName>' lacks explicit resistance R1/type definition or has non-positive length. |
| `PF1003` | warning | `transformer-voltage-mismatch` | Transformer '<trafoName>' rated HV voltage differs by >20% from connected bus nominal voltage. |
| `PF1004` | warning | `generator-voltage-setpoint-bounds` | Generator '<genName>' voltage setpoint is outside typical operating range [0.8, 1.2] pu. |
| `PF1005` | warning | `generator-power-exceeds-mbase` | Generator '<genName>' scheduled active power exceeds rated apparent power MVA. |
| `PF1008` | error | `unresolved-terminal-reference` | Element '<elementName>' references unknown terminal '<terminalId>'. |

---

## 2. Node-Breaker Topology Reduction & DSL Compilation

### Disjoint-Set Bus-Branch Reduction (`processPowerFactoryTopology`)

Substations modeled at the node-breaker level with busbars (`ElmTerm`), circuit breakers (`ElmCoup`), and bay switches (`StaSwitch`) are reduced via union-find partitioning over closed switching devices (`on_off = 1`). Open switches isolate faulted or de-energized busbar sections while preserving active equipment terminal assignments.

### DIgSILENT Simulation Language (`.dsl`) to Modelica & DAE (`transpileDslToModelica`)

Continuous control definitions in `.dsl` (excitation systems, turbine governors, PSS, and wind/PV plant controllers) are parsed into state-space transfer blocks (`select`, `lim`, `lincirlo`, `pictrl`, `lag`, `der`) and lowered into OpenIPSL-compatible Modelica `block` declarations and `DAEBuilder` differential-algebraic equations.

---

## 3. Advanced Grid Analysis: OPF, QDSL, Harmonics, Modes & DLR

- **AC & DC Optimal Power Flow (`solvePowerFactoryOpf`)**: Minimizes generation dispatch cost $\sum (c_2 P_{g,i}^2 + c_1 P_{g,i} + c_0)$ subject to nodal power balance, generator capability bounds, bus voltage limits, and branch MVA thermal ratings.
- **Quasi-Dynamic Simulation (`solvePowerFactoryQdsl`)**: Executes multi-step time-series power flow profiles across diurnal load and solar/wind generation scaling curves.
- **Harmonic Power Flow & Frequency Scans**: Evaluates bus Total Harmonic Distortion ($\text{THD}_V$) against IEEE 519-2022 limits and sweeps driving-point harmonic impedance $Z(h)$ to identify parallel LC resonance peaks.
- **Small-Signal Stability (`modes`)**: Computes electromechanical oscillation modes ($\lambda = \sigma \pm j\omega$, frequency $f$, damping ratio $\zeta = -\sigma / |\lambda|$) via the Sparse Arnoldi Krylov subspace eigensolver or dense QR factorization.
- **IEEE 738 Dynamic Line Rating (`dlr`)**: Solves the steady-state and transient overhead conductor heat balance ($q_c + q_r = q_s + I^2 R(T_c)$) to determine real-time ampacity and thermal emergency ratings.

---

## 4. Command-Line Interface (`msx powerfactory` / `msx pf`)

```bash
# Inspect substation, terminal, line, transformer, and generator counts
msx powerfactory inspect grid.pfd

# Solve AC power flow on a PowerFactory network model
msx powerfactory solve grid.pfd

# Run IEC 60909 three-phase short-circuit fault calculations
msx powerfactory fault grid.pfd

# Compute small-signal stability eigenvalues using the Sparse Arnoldi solver
msx powerfactory modes grid.pfd --method=arnoldi

# Run DC or AC Optimal Power Flow (OPF)
msx powerfactory opf grid.pfd --formulation=dc

# Evaluate IEEE 738 Dynamic Line Rating, harmonic THD, QDSL, and grid-code compliance
msx powerfactory dlr grid.pfd
msx powerfactory harmonics grid.pfd
msx powerfactory qdsl grid.pfd
msx powerfactory gridcode grid.pfd

# Export Single-Line Diagram SVG, PSS/E .raw, or OpenIPSL Modelica .mo
msx powerfactory diagram grid.pfd --out=grid-sld.svg
msx powerfactory to-psse grid.pfd --out=grid.raw
msx powerfactory to-modelica grid.pfd --out=GridModel.mo
```

# GE Vernova PSLF-Compatible WECC Transmission (`.epc`, `.dyd`)

The `@modelscript/pslf` language package (`languages/pslf`) provides native support for **GE Vernova PSLF-compatible** Positive Sequence Load Flow (`.epc`) and Dynamic Simulation Data (`.dyd`) models used across the Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC). It delivers `.epc` and `.dyd` parsing and round-trip serialization, pre-flight WECC topological and dynamic parameter linting (`PSLF-E001`–`PSLF-W003`), non-linear AC power flow solving, and bi-directional conversion between **GE PSLF (`.epc`/`.dyd`)** and **Siemens PTI PSS/E (`.raw`/`.dyr`)** including second-generation WECC renewable energy models (`regca1`, `reeca1`, `repca1`).

---

## Supported File Specifications & Dynamic Models

| Section / Model                      | Format          | Key Structural Features                                                                                      |
| :----------------------------------- | :-------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **`bus` / `branch` / `transformer`** | `.epc` Deck     | Extended bus names, kV base voltages, area/zone/owner numbers, multi-section AC lines, and phase shifters    |
| **`generator` / `load` / `shunt`**   | `.epc` Deck     | Synchronous & IBR dispatch ($P_g, Q_g, Q_{\min}, Q_{\max}, M_{\text{base}}$), ZIP loads, switched SVD shunts |
| **`gencls` / `gentpf` / `gensal`**   | `.dyd` Dynamics | Classical and subtransient salient/round-rotor synchronous machines with saturation and inertia $H$          |
| **`exst1` / `ieeego` / `tgov1`**     | `.dyd` Dynamics | IEEE Type ST1 excitation systems and steam/hydro speed-governing turbine models                              |
| **`regca1` / `reeca1` / `repca1`**   | `.dyd` Dynamics | WECC 2nd-generation renewable generator/converter, electrical control, and plant controller models           |

---

## Architecture & Compilation Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    EPC["GE PSLF Power Flow (.epc)"]
    DYD["GE PSLF Dynamic Data (.dyd)"]

    subgraph FrontEnd["Parser & Static Validation"]
        PEPC["EPC Section Parser & Writer"]
        PDYD["DYD Dynamic Model Parser & Writer"]
        LINT["WECC Topology & Dynamics Linter (PSLF-E001–W003)"]
    end

    subgraph Solvers["Power Flow & Bi-Directional Exchange"]
        SOLVE["Non-Linear AC Power Flow Solver"]
        TOPSSE["PSLF to PSS/E (.raw + .dyr) Translator"]
        FROMPSSE["PSS/E (.raw + .dyr) to PSLF Translator"]
    end

    EPC --> PEPC --> LINT & SOLVE & TOPSSE
    DYD --> PDYD --> LINT & TOPSSE
    FROMPSSE --> PEPC & PDYD
```

---

## 1. Pre-Flight WECC Grid & Dynamic Diagnostic Rules

`@modelscript/pslf` checks `.epc` and `.dyd` decks for missing swing buses, dangling branch/transformer/generator references, inverted reactive capability limits, isolated buses, and invalid machine inertia constants:

### Diagnostics for GE Vernova PSLF (10 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `PSLF-E001` | error | `missing-slack-bus` | No slack / swing bus (busType 3) defined in the power flow case. |
| `PSLF-E002` | error | `dangling-branch-bus` | Transmission line connects to non-existent bus '<busNumber>'. |
| `PSLF-E003` | error | `dangling-transformer-bus` | Transformer connects to non-existent bus '<busNumber>'. |
| `PSLF-E004` | error | `dangling-generator-bus` | Generator is connected to non-existent bus '<busNumber>'. |
| `PSLF-E005` | error | `inverted-generator-reactive-limits` | Generator reactive lower limit Q_min (<qmin> Mvar) exceeds Q_max (<qmax> Mvar). |
| `PSLF-E006` | error | `dangling-dynamic-model-bus` | Dynamic model '<modelType>' refers to non-existent power flow bus '<busNumber>'. |
| `PSLF-E007` | error | `non-positive-generator-inertia` | Classical generator model has non-positive inertia H = '<inertiaH>'. |
| `PSLF-W001` | warning | `non-positive-branch-reactance` | Branch series reactance X is non-positive (<xPu> pu). |
| `PSLF-W002` | warning | `transformer-ratio-out-of-bounds` | Transformer off-nominal turns ratio <ratio> pu is outside typical operating envelope [0.8, 1.2]. |
| `PSLF-W003` | warning | `isolated-bus` | Bus '<busName>' is electrically isolated without any in-service branch or transformer connections. |

---

## 2. Bi-Directional PSLF $\leftrightarrow$ PSS/E Translation

### Power Flow Mapping (`pslfEpcToPsseRaw` / `psseRawToPslfEpc`)

Maps PSLF `.epc` bus, branch, two-winding transformer, generator, load, switched shunt, and area records to PSS/E v33 `.raw` data blocks while preserving per-unit impedances on system $S_{\text{base}}$, transformer complex tap ratios, and reactive power capability bounds.

### WECC Dynamic Model Mapping (`pslfDydToPsseDyr` / `psseDyrToPslfDyd`)

Translates `.dyd` dynamic model records (`gencls`, `gentpf`, `exst1`, `ieeego`, `regca1`, `reeca1`, `repca1`, `wndt`) to and from PSS/E `.dyr` `CON` parameter arrays, aligning generator bus numbers, machine IDs, and MVA base ratings.

---

## 3. Command-Line Interface (`msx pslf`)

```bash
# Inspect bus, generator, load, line, transformer, and dynamic model counts
msx pslf inspect wecc_case.epc
msx pslf summary wecc_case.epc

# Run pre-flight topological and dynamic parameter lint checks
msx pslf lint wecc_case.epc wecc_case.dyd

# Solve AC power flow on a GE PSLF .epc case
msx pslf solve wecc_case.epc

# Convert GE PSLF (.epc / .dyd) to PSS/E (.raw / .dyr)
msx pslf to-psse wecc_case.epc --dyr=wecc_case.dyd --out=wecc_case.raw

# Convert PSS/E (.raw / .dyr) to GE PSLF (.epc / .dyd)
msx pslf from-psse wecc_case.raw --dyr=wecc_case.dyr --out=wecc_case.epc
```

# CIM / CGMES European Grid Exchange (`.xml`, `.rdf`)

The `@modelscript/cgmes` language package (`languages/cgmes`) provides native ingestion, node-breaker topology processing, semantic validation (`C1001`–`C1010`), AC/DC Optimal Power Flow (OPF) solving, and multi-domain projection for the **ENTSO-E Common Grid Model Exchange Standard (CGMES v2.4.15 & v3.0 / IEC 61970-600-2)**. It parses multi-file CIM RDF/XML datasets across Equipment (`EQ`), Topology (`TP`), Steady State Hypothesis (`SSH`), and State Variables (`SV`) profiles, resolves ConnectivityNode/TopologicalNode graphs via disjoint-set Union-Find, and projects European transmission grids directly to **PSS/E (`.raw`)** and **OpenIPSL Modelica (`.mo`)**.

<LanguageExample lang="cgmes" />

---

## Supported CIM / CGMES Profiles

| Profile                             | IEC 61970 Namespace            | Core CIM Classes Indexed                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| :---------------------------------- | :----------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Equipment (`EQ`)**                | `EquipmentProfile`             | `Substation`, `VoltageLevel`, `BaseVoltage`, `ConnectivityNode`, `Terminal`, `ACLineSegment`, `PowerTransformer`, `PowerTransformerEnd`, `SynchronousMachine`, `EnergyConsumer`, `LinearShuntCompensator` |
| **Topology (`TP`)**                 | `TopologyProfile`              | `TopologicalNode`, `Terminal.TopologicalNode` bindings, busbar section assignments                                                                                                                        |
| **Steady State Hypothesis (`SSH`)** | `SteadyStateHypothesisProfile` | `RotatingMachine.p`, `RotatingMachine.q`, `EnergyConsumer.p`, `EnergyConsumer.q`, `LinearShuntCompensator.sections`, breaker states                                                                       |
| **State Variables (`SV`)**          | `StateVariablesProfile`        | `SvVoltage` ($V_{\text{pu}}, \theta_{\text{deg}}$), `SvPowerFlow` ($P, Q$ terminal flows)                                                                                                                 |

---

## Architecture & Compilation Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Profiles["IEC 61970-600-2 Multi-Profile Dataset"]
        EQ["EQ Profile (Equipment .xml/.rdf)"]
        TP["TP Profile (Topology .xml/.rdf)"]
        SSH["SSH Profile (Steady State Hypothesis)"]
        SV["SV Profile (State Variables)"]
    end

    subgraph Engine["@modelscript/cgmes Core Engine"]
        PARSER["Multi-Profile RDF/XML Merger (parseCgmesFiles)"]
        TOPO["Union-Find Topology Processor (processTopology)"]
        LINT["ENTSO-E Semantic Linter (C1001–C1010)"]
    end

    subgraph Projections["Projections & Power Flow Solvers"]
        PSSE["PSS/E Base Case (cgmesToPsse)"]
        MO["OpenIPSL Modelica Package (cgmesToModelica)"]
        SOLVE["NR / HELM / DC-OPF / AC-OPF Solvers"]
    end

    EQ & TP & SSH & SV --> PARSER
    PARSER --> TOPO
    TOPO --> LINT
    TOPO --> PSSE & MO
    PSSE --> SOLVE
```

---

## 1. Disjoint-Set Topology Processing & Per-Unit Conversion

### Node-Breaker to Bus-Branch Synthesis (`processTopology`)

European TSO datasets frequently mix bus-branch (`TopologicalNode`) and node-breaker (`ConnectivityNode`) representations across voltage levels. `processTopology()` constructs a path-compressed, union-by-rank `DisjointSet` forest over all `TopologicalNode` and `ConnectivityNode` identifiers:

1. **Terminal Equivalence Unification**: For every `cim:Terminal` referencing both a `connectivityNodeId` ($c_k$) and a `topologicalNodeId` ($n_m$), the processor executes $\text{Union}(c_k, n_m)$.
2. **Synthetic Bus Synthesis**: When a connected component root $r = \text{Find}(c_k)$ lacks an explicit `TP` `TopologicalNode`, `processTopology()` synthesizes a canonical `TopologicalNode` inheriting its nominal voltage $V_{\text{base}}$ from the enclosing `cim:VoltageLevel`.
3. **Electrical Island Detection**: A second disjoint-set pass unions all nodes bridged by energized `ACLineSegment` and multi-winding `PowerTransformer` terminals to compute `islandCount` and flag isolated substations (`C1009`).

### Per-Unit Impedance & Thermal Rating Normalization

During projection to PSS/E (`cgmesToPsse`) on system MVA base $S_{\text{base}} = 100\text{ MVA}$, physical engineering quantities from `EQ` profiles are normalized using the nominal voltage $V_{\text{base}}$ ($\text{kV}$) of the terminal's `TopologicalNode`. First, the base impedance is computed from the nominal line-to-line voltage and system base power:

$$Z_{\text{base}} = \frac{V_{\text{base}}^2}{S_{\text{base}}} \quad [\Omega]$$

For an `ACLineSegment`, physical resistance, reactance, and charging susceptance are converted to dimensionless per-unit values, and the thermal current limit is converted to an apparent power rating (`Rate A`):

$$r_{\text{pu}} = \frac{R_{\Omega}}{Z_{\text{base}}}, \qquad x_{\text{pu}} = \frac{X_{\Omega}}{Z_{\text{base}}}, \qquad b_{\text{pu}} = B_{\text{ch}} \cdot Z_{\text{base}}$$

$$\text{Rate A} = \frac{\sqrt{3} \, V_{\text{base}} \, I_{\max}}{1000} \quad [\text{MVA}]$$

For a `LinearShuntCompensator` with $N_{\text{sec}}$ energized sections, the total nominal active and reactive power injection at $1.0\text{ pu}$ voltage is obtained by scaling the per-section admittance by the squared nominal voltage:

$$G_{\text{shunt}} + j B_{\text{shunt}} = N_{\text{sec}} \left( g_{\text{sec}} + j b_{\text{sec}} \right) V_{\text{base}}^2 \quad [\text{MW} + j\,\text{MVAr}]$$

| Symbol                                        | Meaning                                                                      | Units / Domain                              |
| :-------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------ |
| $Z_{\text{base}}$                             | Base impedance at the bus nominal voltage                                    | $\Omega$ ($> 0$)                            |
| $V_{\text{base}}$                             | Nominal line-to-line voltage of the `TopologicalNode`                        | $\text{kV}$ ($> 0$)                         |
| $S_{\text{base}}$                             | System three-phase apparent power base ($100\text{ MVA}$)                    | $\text{MVA}$ ($> 0$)                        |
| $r_{\text{pu}}, x_{\text{pu}}, b_{\text{pu}}$ | Per-unit series resistance, series reactance, and shunt charging susceptance | Dimensionless ($\text{pu}$)                 |
| $R_{\Omega}, X_{\Omega}$                      | Physical ohmic resistance and reactance of the line segment                  | $\Omega$                                    |
| $B_{\text{ch}}$                               | Total physical line charging susceptance                                     | $\text{S}$ (Siemens)                        |
| $\text{Rate A}$                               | Normal thermal apparent power rating                                         | $\text{MVA}$                                |
| $I_{\max}$                                    | Maximum continuous phase current rating                                      | $\text{A}$                                  |
| $G_{\text{shunt}}, B_{\text{shunt}}$          | Nominal shunt active power and reactive power at $1.0\text{ pu}$ voltage     | $\text{MW}, \text{MVAr}$                    |
| $N_{\text{sec}}$                              | Number of energized shunt compensator sections                               | Non-negative integer ($\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$) |
| $g_{\text{sec}}, b_{\text{sec}}$              | Per-section shunt conductance and susceptance                                | $\text{S}$ (Siemens)                        |
| $j$                                           | Imaginary unit ($\sqrt{-1}$)                                                 | Dimensionless                               |

---

## 2. Pre-Flight ENTSO-E CGMES Diagnostic Rules

`@modelscript/cgmes` validates multi-profile referential integrity, equipment physical bounds, and network connectivity before power-flow solving or Modelica code generation:

### Diagnostics for CIM / CGMES (10 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `C1001` | error | `missing-mrid` | TopologicalNode has empty or missing mRID. |
| `C1002` | error | `orphan-terminal` | Terminal '<terminal>' references non-existent ConductingEquipment '<conductingEquipment>'. |
| `C1003` | warning | `dangling-node` | TopologicalNode '<node>' has no connected equipment terminals. |
| `C1004` | error | `invalid-voltage-level` | VoltageLevel '<voltageLevel>' has non-positive base voltage (<baseVoltageKv> kV). |
| `C1005` | error | `transformer-end-mismatch` | PowerTransformer '<transformer>' must have 2 or 3 ends, but found <ends>. |
| `C1006` | error | `generator-limit-inversion` | SynchronousMachine '<generator>' minP (<minP> MW) exceeds maxP (<maxP> MW). |
| `C1007` | warning | `zero-impedance-line` | ACLineSegment '<line>' has zero or negative impedance (r=<r>, x=<x>). |
| `C1008` | info | `negative-load` | EnergyConsumer '<load>' has negative active power (<pMw> MW), behaving as net generation. |
| `C1009` | warning | `isolated-substation` | Substation '<substation>' is isolated from the transmission network. |
| `C1010` | error | `unbalanced-profile-data` | State variable SvVoltage '<svId>' references non-existent TopologicalNode '<topologicalNodeId>'. |

---

## 3. Multi-Domain Projections (`PSS/E` & `OpenIPSL Modelica`)

### Projection to PSS/E (`cgmesToPsse`)

`cgmesToPsse()` maps every resolved `TopologicalNode` to a sequential PSS/E Revision 33 bus number ($1 \dots N$), populates initial voltage magnitudes and phase angles $(V_m, V_a)$ from `SvVoltage` records, assigns `BusType.PV` to generator-regulated buses and `BusType.Swing` to the largest synchronous resource, and assembles `PsseCase` records ready for Newton-Raphson (`nr`), Holomorphic Embedding (`helm`), DC-OPF (`dc-opf`), or nonlinear interior-point AC-OPF (`ac-opf`).

### Projection to OpenIPSL Modelica (`cgmesToModelica`)

`cgmesToModelica()` emits a complete, strongly-typed **OpenIPSL** acausal Modelica package for time-domain electromechanical transient stability studies:

```modelica
package CgmesGridPackage
  model TransmissionSystem
    "CGMES Transformed Network Model"

    // --- Topological Buses ---
    OpenIPSL.Electrical.Buses.Bus Bus_Alpha_380(V_nom = 380000.0);
    OpenIPSL.Electrical.Buses.Bus Bus_Beta_380(V_nom = 380000.0);

    // --- Generators ---
    OpenIPSL.Electrical.Machines.PSSE.GENSAL NuclearUnit_1200MW(
      P_0 = 1150000000.0, Q_0 = 220000000.0, S_nom = 1350000000.0);

    // --- Loads ---
    OpenIPSL.Electrical.Loads.PSSE.Load MetroHub_Beta_Load(
      P_0 = 820000000.0, Q_0 = 195000000.0);

    // --- AC Transmission Lines ---
    OpenIPSL.Electrical.Branches.Line TieLine_Alpha_Beta_380kV(
      R = 1.85000, X = 24.60000, B = 0.00032);

  equation
    connect(NuclearUnit_1200MW.p, Bus_Alpha_380.p);
    connect(MetroHub_Beta_Load.p, Bus_Beta_380.p);
    connect(TieLine_Alpha_Beta_380kV.p, Bus_Alpha_380.p);
    connect(TieLine_Alpha_Beta_380kV.q, Bus_Beta_380.p);
  end TransmissionSystem;
end CgmesGridPackage;
```

## 4. Command-Line Interface (`msx cgmes`)

### Actions

| Action        | Description                                                                                            |
| :------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `inspect`     | Parse EQ/TP/SSH/SV profiles, resolve Union-Find topology, and print element & electrical island counts |
| `lint`        | Run ENTSO-E CGMES static validation rules (`C1001`–`C1010`) across merged profiles                     |
| `to-psse`     | Project the merged CGMES dataset into a PSS/E Revision 33 transmission power-flow base case            |
| `to-modelica` | Synthesize an OpenIPSL acausal Modelica transmission grid model (`.mo`)                                |
| `solve`       | Solve steady-state power flow or Optimal Power Flow (`nr`, `helm`, `dc-opf`, `ac-opf`)                 |

### Options

| Option                       | Description                                                                                      |
| :--------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-o, --out, --output <path>` | Target output file path for exported Modelica models                                             |
| `--alg <name>`               | Solver algorithm for the `solve` action: `nr`, `helm`, `dc-opf`, or `ac-opf` (default: `ac-opf`) |

### Example CLI Session

```bash
# Inspect merged EQ, TP, SSH, and SV profiles and count electrical islands
msx cgmes inspect grid_EQ.xml grid_TP.xml grid_SSH.xml grid_SV.xml

# Validate multi-profile referential integrity and equipment limits (C1001–C1010)
msx cgmes lint grid_EQ.xml grid_TP.xml grid_SSH.xml grid_SV.xml

# Project CGMES network to a PSS/E base case summary
msx cgmes to-psse grid_EQ.xml grid_TP.xml grid_SSH.xml

# Export an OpenIPSL Modelica package for transient stability simulation
msx cgmes to-modelica grid_EQ.xml grid_TP.xml grid_SSH.xml --out=TransmissionGrid.mo

# Solve AC Optimal Power Flow (or Newton-Raphson / HELM / DC-OPF)
msx cgmes solve grid_EQ.xml grid_TP.xml grid_SSH.xml --alg=ac-opf
msx cgmes solve grid_EQ.xml grid_TP.xml grid_SSH.xml --alg=nr
```

## 5. Programmatic TypeScript SDK

```typescript
import { parseCgmesFiles, processTopology, lintCgmesModel, cgmesToPsse, cgmesToModelica } from "@modelscript/cgmes";
import { solvePowerFlow } from "@modelscript/psse";

// 1. Parse and merge EQ, TP, SSH, and SV XML/RDF profile strings
const model = parseCgmesFiles([eqXml, tpXml, sshXml, svXml]);

// 2. Run Union-Find node-breaker to bus-branch topology resolution
const topo = processTopology(model);
console.log(`Resolved ${topo.model.nodes.size} buses across ${topo.islandCount} island(s)`);

// 3. Validate against ENTSO-E CGMES rules C1001–C1010
const diagnostics = lintCgmesModel(model);

// 4. Project to PSS/E and solve AC Power Flow or export OpenIPSL Modelica
const { psseCase } = cgmesToPsse(model, { sbaseMva: 100.0 });
const solution = solvePowerFlow(psseCase, { algorithm: "newton_raphson" });
const modelicaSource = cgmesToModelica(model, { packageName: "EntsoeCorridor" });
```

# OpenDSS Distribution Grids & DERs (`.dss`)

`@modelscript/opendss` (`languages/opendss`) provides zero-regex parsing, unbalanced multi-phase power flow solving, distributed energy resource (DER) hosting capacity analysis, linear DAE lowering, and Modelica 3.x projection for **EPRI OpenDSS** radial and meshed electrical distribution networks.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format               | Description                                                                                     |
| :-------- | :------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.dss`    | OpenDSS Command Deck | Distribution grid feeders, multi-phase line codes, transformers, distributed PV/wind, and loads |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Multi-Phase Unbalanced AC Power Flow

- Solves unbalanced radial and weakly meshed 3-phase/4-wire distribution networks via the **nodal admittance matrix ($Y_{\text{bus}}$)** formulation and **Forward-Backward Sweep (FBS)**, relating bus current injections to bus voltages and computing constant-power load currents:
  $$I_{\text{inj}}(V) = Y_{\text{bus}} V$$
  $$I_i(V_i) = \left( \frac{P_i + j Q_i}{V_i} \right)^*$$

  | Symbol              | Meaning                                                       | Units / Domain                            |
  | :------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------ | :---------------------------------------- |
  | $I_{\text{inj}}(V)$ | Vector of complex nodal current injections                    | $\text{A}$ (or $\text{p.u.}$)             |
  | $Y_{\text{bus}}$    | Complex nodal admittance matrix                               | $\text{S}$ (or $\text{p.u.}$)             |
  | $V, V_i$            | Vector of complex bus voltages and voltage phasor at node $i$ | $\text{V}$ (or $\text{p.u.}$)             |
  | $I_i(V_i)$          | Complex load current drawn at node $i$                        | $\text{A}$ (or $\text{p.u.}$)             |
  | $P_i, Q_i$          | Active and reactive power demand at node $i$                  | $\text{W}, \text{VAr}$ (or $\text{p.u.}$) |
  | $j, (\cdot)^*$      | Imaginary unit ($\sqrt{-1}$) and complex conjugate operator   | $\text{dimensionless}$                    |

- Accurately tracks mutual coupling across multi-conductor overhead lines and underground concentric neutral cables using Carson's equations for earth return path impedance.

### 2. DER Hosting Capacity & Reverse Power Flow

- Models distributed solar photovoltaic (PVSystem) generators, battery energy storage systems (Storage), and wind generators.
- Analyzes thermal line loading limits and voltage regulation limits (ANSI C84.1 Range A: $0.95 \le |V| \le 1.05\text{ p.u.}$), estimating the steady-state feeder voltage rise induced by distributed energy resource (DER) active and reactive injection:
  $$\Delta V \approx \frac{R P_{\text{DER}} + X Q_{\text{DER}}}{V_0}$$

  | Symbol                           | Meaning                                                            | Units / Domain                            |
  | :------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------- |
  | $\Delta V$                       | Approximate voltage magnitude rise at the point of interconnection | $\text{V}$ (or $\text{p.u.}$)             |
  | $R, X$                           | Equivalent upstream feeder resistance and reactance                | $\Omega$ (or $\text{p.u.}$)               |
  | $P_{\text{DER}}, Q_{\text{DER}}$ | Net active and reactive power injected by the DER                  | $\text{W}, \text{VAr}$ (or $\text{p.u.}$) |
  | $V_0$                            | Nominal (no-load) feeder voltage magnitude                         | $\text{V}$ (or $\text{p.u.}$)             |

- Identifies reverse power flow hazards where generation exceeds local demand, pushing power back through substation transformers into the transmission bulk grid ([`@modelscript/psse`](./psse.md)).

### 3. Direct DAE Lowering

- Compiles lines, transformers, and voltage-dependent loads into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` linear memory arena.
- Enables co-simulation between distribution feeders, electromagnetic transients in inverter controllers ([`@modelscript/pscad`](./pscad.md)), and building thermal energy consumption ([`@modelscript/energyplus`](./energyplus.md)).

### 4. Faults, Harmonics, Protection, IEEE 1366 Reliability, GIC & FLISR

- **Distribution OPF (`opf`), Short-Circuit (`fault`), and Harmonics (`harmonics`)**: Evaluates DER Volt-Var/curtailment dispatch, unbalanced phase-to-ground and 3-phase fault currents, and harmonic distortion profiles.
- **Protection Coordination (`protection`), IEEE 1366 Reliability (`reliability`), GIC (`gic`) & FLISR (`flisr`)**: Audits fuse-recloser coordination, computes SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI indices, evaluates geomagnetic induced currents, and identifies optimal tie-switch sectionalizing for Fault Location, Isolation, and Service Restoration.

### 5. Bidirectional Modelica 3.x Projection

- Projects OpenDSS circuits into standard multi-phase Modelica or OpenIPSL electrical network models with acausal electrical pins (`v`, `i`).

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

The OpenDSS linter verifies electrical connectivity and DER operating envelopes:

### Diagnostics for OpenDSS (13 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M8401` | error | `unconnected-bus-node` | <elemType> '<elemName>' references undefined bus node '<busName>'. |
| `M8402` | error | `transformer-impedance-zero` | Transformer '<xfmrName>' specifies non-positive leakage reactance (xhl=<xhl>); must be > 0. |
| `M8403` | warning | `load-pf-out-of-range` | Load '<loadName>' specifies power factor (<pf>) outside valid range (0 < \|pf\| <= 1.0). |
| `M8404` | warning | `reverse-power-hosting-risk` | Total DER generation capacity on feeder '<feederName>' (<value> kW) exceeds upstream transformer thermal rating (<value> kVA). |
| `M8405` | error | `missing-circuit-definition` | OpenDSS script defines circuit elements without declaring a 'New Circuit' voltage source. |
| `M8406` | error | `negative-load-power` | Load '<loadName>' specifies negative active power (<value> kW); use Generator or Storage for net generation. |
| `M8407` | error | `zero-or-negative-line-length` | Line '<lineName>' specifies invalid non-positive length (<len>). |
| `M8408` | error | `missing-line-code` | Line '<lineName>' references undefined LineCode '<codeName>'. |
| `M8409` | error | `phase-count-mismatch` | Element '<elemName>' (<elemPhases> phases) connected to bus '<busName>' with different phase count (<busPhases>). |
| `M8410` | warning | `transformer-voltage-mismatch` | Transformer '<xfmrName>' winding <winding> rated voltage (<value> kV) differs from nominal bus voltage (<value> kV). |
| `M8411` | error | `isolated-island-no-slack` | Distribution subnetwork island has no reference slack bus or grid-forming inverter. |
| `M8412` | error | `non-positive-definite-zmatrix` | Line '<lineName>' impedance matrix is not positive-definite. |
| `M8413` | warning | `capacitor-overvoltage-risk` | Capacitor bank '<capName>' kVAR rating (<kvar>) exceeds feeder minimum load (<loadKvar>), risking overvoltage. |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Inspect distribution buses, lines, transformers, and DER units
msx opendss inspect IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss
msx opendss summary IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss

# Run pre-flight linting and connectivity verification
msx opendss lint IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss

# Solve multi-phase AC power flow (FBS or sparse Ybus) and distribution OPF
msx opendss powerflow IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss
msx opendss ybus IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss
msx opendss opf IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss

# Run fault study, harmonics, protection, IEEE 1366 reliability, GIC, hosting capacity, and FLISR
msx opendss fault IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss --bus=671
msx opendss harmonics IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss
msx opendss protection IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss
msx opendss reliability IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss
msx opendss gic IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss
msx opendss hosting-capacity IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss --bus=671
msx opendss flisr IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss --bus=671

# Lower circuit into ModelScript linear DAE arena or Modelica 3.x
msx opendss to-dae IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss
msx opendss to-modelica IEEE13NodeFeeder.dss -o DistributionFeeder.mo
```

# OCPP EV Smart Charging (`.ocpp`, `.json`)

`@modelscript/ocpp` (`languages/ocpp`) provides native parsing, priority load allocation, transformer headroom constraint checking, and linear DAE lowering for **Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP 2.0.1 / 1.6J)** electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) networks and fleet depots.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format                  | Description                                                            |
| :-------- | :---------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.ocpp`   | OCPP Network Manifest   | Station hierarchy, EVSE connector ratings, and charging session states |
| `.json`   | OCPP 2.0.1 JSON Payload | JSON schema conforming EV charging schedules and composite profiles    |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Urgency-Weighted Smart Charging Allocation

- Dynamically schedules active vehicle sessions under a shared transformer or feeder capacity limit $P_{\text{grid}}^{\max}$, prioritizing sessions by energy urgency relative to remaining dwell time:
  $$\sum_{i=1}^{N_{\text{active}}} P_i(t) \le P_{\text{grid}}^{\max}$$
  $$U_i = \frac{E_{\text{req},i}}{\max(0.1, t_{\text{dep},i} - t)}$$
  where $E_{\text{req},i} = (SoC_{\text{target},i} - SoC_{\text{current},i}) \cdot C_{\text{battery},i}$ is the remaining energy required and $P_i(t) \le P_{\text{conn},i}^{\max}$ enforces hardware connector physical maximums.

  | Symbol                   | Meaning                                                  | Units / Domain                                             |
  | :----------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------- |
  | $i, N_{\text{active}}$   | Session index and number of active charging sessions     | $\text{dimensionless}$ ($i = 1, \dots, N_{\text{active}}$) |
  | $P_i(t)$                 | Charging power allocated to session $i$ at time $t$      | $\text{kW}$ ($P_i \ge 0$)                                  |
  | $P_{\text{grid}}^{\max}$ | Maximum aggregate site/feeder power limit                | $\text{kW}$                                                |
  | $U_i$                    | Charging urgency score for session $i$                   | $\text{kW}$                                                |
  | $E_{\text{req},i}$       | Remaining energy needed to reach target state of charge  | $\text{kWh}$                                               |
  | $t_{\text{dep},i}, t$    | Scheduled departure time of vehicle $i$ and current time | $\text{h}$                                                 |

### 2. Multi-Tier Profile Priority Hierarchy

- Implements the standard OCPP charging profile stack:
  1. `ChargePointMaxProfile` (overall site ceiling)
  2. `TxDefaultProfile` (station default tariff/limit schedule)
  3. `TxProfile` (session-specific dynamically injected profile)
- Integrates with power distribution models (`@modelscript/opendss`) and transit fleet schedules (`@modelscript/gtfs`).

### 3. DAE Formulation for Transformer Overload Protection

- Lowers aggregated EVSE power and battery state-of-charge dynamics into `DAEBuilder`, integrating charging power into battery state of charge and summing site demand:
  $$\frac{d(SoC_i)}{dt} = \frac{\eta_{\text{chg}} \cdot P_i(t)}{C_{\text{battery},i}}$$
  $$P_{\text{total}}(t) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} P_i(t)$$

  | Symbol                 | Meaning                                       | Units / Domain                                         |
  | :--------------------- | :-------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------- |
  | $SoC_i$                | State of charge of vehicle battery $i$        | $\text{dimensionless}$ ($0 \le SoC_i \le 1$)           |
  | $t$                    | Simulation time                               | $\text{h}$                                             |
  | $\eta_{\text{chg}}$    | Charger-to-battery conversion efficiency      | $\text{dimensionless}$ ($0 < \eta_{\text{chg}} \le 1$) |
  | $P_i(t)$               | Charging power delivered to vehicle $i$       | $\text{kW}$                                            |
  | $C_{\text{battery},i}$ | Usable battery energy capacity of vehicle $i$ | $\text{kWh}$                                           |
  | $P_{\text{total}}(t)$  | Total aggregate power drawn by all $N$ EVSEs  | $\text{kW}$                                            |
  | $N$                    | Total number of EVSE connectors at the site   | $\text{dimensionless}$                                 |

- Emits soft-slack penalty equations for transformer thermal capacity overloads.

---

| `M3002` | error | `ocpp-invalid-soc-range` | Charging session '<txId>' has invalid SoC range: current <currentSoC>, target <targetSoC>. Values must be in [0.0, 1.0] with target > current. |
| `M4001` | error | `ocpp-connector-not-found` | EVSE '<evseId>', connector '<connId>' in station '<stationId>' has invalid ID (must be positive integer). |
