# RAN & Microwave Propagation (`.adf`, `.pat`, ITU-R P.530)

`@modelscript/ran` (`languages/ran`) provides antenna pattern ingestion, 3D envelope synthesis, and microwave link propagation modeling for **cellular Radio Access Networks (4G/5G), fixed wireless access (FWA), and utility microwave backhaul**.

---

## Supported Standards & Formats

| Format / Standard       | File Extensions | Description                                                                                              |
| :---------------------- | :-------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **NSMA WG16.99.050**    | `.adf`, `.nsma` | National Spectrum Management Association standardized antenna radiation patterns (azimuth and elevation) |
| **Planet / TIA-329**    | `.pat`, `.msi`  | Industry-standard Planet and TIA-329 antenna pattern decks                                               |
| **ITU-R P.530-18**      | Specification   | International Telecommunication Union rain fade attenuation and availability prediction                  |
| **ITU-R P.838 / P.837** | Specification   | Specific rain attenuation coefficients ($\gamma = k R^\alpha$) and digital rain maps                     |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. 2D/3D Antenna Radiation Pattern Interpolation

- Parses dual-polarized horizontal and vertical antenna gain cuts across $360^\circ$ azimuth and $\pm 90^\circ$ elevation.
- Computes half-power beamwidth (HPBW, 3 dB) and front-to-back (F/B) ratios.
- Bicubic 3D gain envelope interpolation combines horizontal and tilted vertical pattern cuts, capped by the front-to-back attenuation floor:
  $$G(\theta, \phi) = G_{\text{peak}} - \min\left(-(A_H(\phi) + A_V(\theta - \theta_{\text{tilt}})), A_m\right)$$

  | Symbol                               | Meaning                                                                         | Units / Domain       |
  | :----------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :------------------- |
  | $G(\theta, \phi)$                    | 3D directional antenna gain at elevation $\theta$ and azimuth $\phi$            | $\text{dBi}$         |
  | $G_{\text{peak}}$                    | Maximum boresight antenna gain                                                  | $\text{dBi}$         |
  | $A_H(\phi)$                          | Horizontal (azimuth) relative attenuation pattern                               | $\text{dB}$, $\le 0$ |
  | $A_V(\theta - \theta_{\text{tilt}})$ | Vertical (elevation) relative attenuation shifted by downtilt                   | $\text{dB}$, $\le 0$ |
  | $\theta, \phi$                       | Elevation ($[-90^\circ, 90^\circ]$) and azimuth ($[0^\circ, 360^\circ)$) angles | $^\circ$             |
  | $\theta_{\text{tilt}}$               | Combined electrical and mechanical downtilt angle                               | $^\circ$             |
  | $A_m$                                | Maximum front-to-back attenuation cap                                           | $\text{dB}$, $> 0$   |

### 2. Microwave Link Budget & ITU-R P.530 Rain Fade

- Computes Free Space Path Loss (FSPL) over an unobstructed line-of-sight path and atmospheric absorption:
  $$\text{FSPL}(\text{dB}) = 20 \log_{10}(d) + 20 \log_{10}(f) + 92.45$$
  where $\text{FSPL}$ is the free-space path loss ($\text{dB}$), $d$ is the link distance ($\text{km}$, $> 0$), and $f$ is the carrier frequency ($\text{GHz}$, $> 0$).
- Solves ITU-R P.530-18 rain attenuation for $0.01\%$ of time ($A_{0.01} = \gamma_R \cdot d_{\text{eff}}$) and annual link availability percent (verifying "five-nines" $99.999\%$ uptime).

### 3. Fresnel Zone Clearance & Earth Curvature

- Computes the 1st Fresnel zone radius enclosing the primary radio-frequency energy ellipsoid along the propagation path:
  $$F_1 = 17.32 \sqrt{\frac{d_1 d_2}{f \cdot D}}$$

  | Symbol     | Meaning                                           | Units / Domain      |
  | :--------- | :------------------------------------------------ | :------------------ |
  | $F_1$      | First Fresnel zone radius at the obstacle         | $\text{m}$, $> 0$   |
  | $d_1, d_2$ | Distances from the obstacle to each link endpoint | $\text{km}$, $> 0$  |
  | $D$        | Total link path length ($D = d_1 + d_2$)          | $\text{km}$, $> 0$  |
  | $f$        | Carrier frequency                                 | $\text{GHz}$, $> 0$ |

- Evaluates Earth curvature bulge ($h_{\text{bulge}} = \frac{d_1 d_2}{12.74 k}$) using effective Earth radius factor $k = 4/3$.
- Identifies terrain and obstacle obstructions where clearance ratio falls below the $0.60 F_1$ threshold.

### 4. FCC OET Bulletin 65 & ICNIRP 2020 RF Radiation Safety (MPE)

- Computes near-field and far-field power density ($S = \frac{\text{EIRP}}{4\pi R^2}$ with ground reflection) across multi-operator colocation sites.
- Evaluates occupational/controlled and general-public/uncontrolled Maximum Permissible Exposure (MPE) horizontal and vertical exclusion boundaries.

### 5. FAA 14 CFR Part 77, ICAO Annex 14 & Transport Canada Airspace Obstruction

- Evaluates proposed cellular and microwave towers against FAA Part 77 imaginary surfaces (primary, approach, transitional, horizontal, conical), 200-ft AGL notice criteria, ICAO Annex 14 Obstacle Limitation Surfaces (OLS), and Transport Canada TP 312 / CAR 601.

---

# Fiber Outside Plant & SRLG Cadastre (TIA-598-D, GeoJSON)

`@modelscript/fiber` (`languages/fiber`) provides outside plant (OSP) civil infrastructure modeling, strand-level optical routing, and physical route diversity analysis for **telecom carriers, metro fiber utilities, and critical infrastructure networks**.

---

## Supported Standards & Formats

| Format / Standard        | File Extensions     | Description                                                                                              |
| :----------------------- | :------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ANSI/TIA-598-D**       | Specification       | Standardized optical fiber cable color coding (12-color sequence) for buffer tubes, ribbons, and strands |
| **GeoJSON OSP Cadastre** | `.geojson`, `.json` | Geographic Outside Plant network schema for cables, ducts, utility poles, manholes, and splice closures  |
| **SRLG Risk Models**     | `.json`             | Shared Risk Link Group specifications for physical routing diversity verification                        |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. ANSI/TIA-598-D 12-Color Registry

- Full resolution of standard telecom color sequence:
  1. Blue, 2. Orange, 3. Green, 4. Brown, 5. Slate, 6. White, 7. Red, 8. Black, 9. Yellow, 10. Violet, 11. Rose, 12. Aqua.
- Hierarchical identification of high-count cables (up to 864+ fibers) with striped buffer tubes and bundle binders.

### 2. Multi-Hop Optical Strand Tracing

- Traces continuous optical lightpaths from Central Office (CO) Optical Distribution Frames (ODF) across cables, patch panels, and fusion splices down to customer demarcation points.
- Accounts for fusion splice insertion loss, connector reflections, and cable sheath lengths.

### 3. Shared Risk Link Group (SRLG) Disjointness

- Evaluates physical path isolation between primary and backup protection circuits, ensuring the two routes share no common physical failure-domain risk groups (ducts, poles, trenches, or manholes):
  $$\text{SRLG}(P_{\text{primary}}) \cap \text{SRLG}(P_{\text{backup}}) = \emptyset$$
  where $P_{\text{primary}}$ and $P_{\text{backup}}$ are the primary and backup optical path sequences of links/nodes, and $\text{SRLG}(P)$ is the set of Shared Risk Link Group identifiers traversed by path $P$.
- Detects physical Single Points of Failure (SPOFs) where supposedly diverse customer circuits share common trenches, duct banks, utility poles, or bridge crossings.
- Calculates Jaccard physical diversity scores.

### 4. OTDR-to-GIS GPS Fault Geolocation

- Pinpoints the physical GPS latitude/longitude of fiber breaks or high-loss anomalies detected by OTDR traces.
- Applies cable helical twisting correction factor ($H = 1.01$–$1.05$) to convert measured optical glass length into true physical cable sheath distance:
  $$d_{\text{physical}} = \frac{d_{\text{optical}}}{H}$$
  where $d_{\text{physical}}$ is the physical cable sheath distance ($\text{m}$ or $\text{km}$, $\ge 0$), $d_{\text{optical}}$ is the OTDR-measured optical fiber length ($\text{m}$ or $\text{km}$, $\ge 0$), and $H$ is the dimensionless helical stranding / excess-fiber-length factor ($H \ge 1$).
- Corrects for slack storage coils stored in vaults, manholes, and aerial snowshoes.
- Identifies the closest upstream and downstream access enclosures to dispatch emergency restoration crews directly to the proper vault.

### 5. NESC C2 Pole Loading, Make-Ready & FCC BDC H3 Fabric

- Solves aerial catenary sag-tension under NESC Heavy, Medium, Light, and Extreme Wind loading zones, and audits utility pole ground-line bending moment utilization and NESC Rule 235/238 vertical communication-to-supply clearances (plus CSA C22.3 No. 1 and Eurocode EN 1991-1-4).
- Discretizes fiber service polygons into Uber H3 resolution-8/9/10 hexagonal cells (`discretizeCoverageToH3`) for FCC Broadband Data Collection (BDC) filings.

---

## Pre-Flight Outside Plant Lint Rules

| `FIBER1002` | error | `unresolved-node-reference` | Cable '<cableId>' references non-existent structure node '<nodeId>'. |
| `FIBER1003` | warning | `excessive-splice-loss` | Splice '<spliceId>' estimated loss (<lossDb> dB) exceeds ITU-T/TIA standard threshold of <maxLossDb> dB. |
| `FIBER1004` | error | `invalid-strand-count` | Cable '<cableId>' strand count (<count>) is not a positive multiple of fibers-per-tube (<perTube>). |

# URDF & Xacro Robot Kinematics

ModelScript provides first-class support for **URDF** (`.urdf`) and **Xacro** (`.xacro`), the robotics industry and ROS (Robot Operating System) standard for describing kinematic trees, inertial properties, visual geometry, and joint limits of robotic manipulators, humanoids, and autonomous vehicles.

---

## Capabilities & Supported Formats

| Format                               | Extension       | Description                                                                                                                                                       |
| :----------------------------------- | :-------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Unified Robot Description Format** | `.urdf`, `.xml` | XML schema defining kinematic links, joints (revolute, continuous, prismatic, fixed, floating, planar), inertial parameters, collision bounds, and visual meshes. |
| **Xacro Macro Template**             | `.xacro`        | Parametric XML preprocessor adding variables (`<xacro:property>`), mathematical expressions, and reusable macros (`<xacro:macro>`).                               |

### Key Architectural Features

- **Xacro Expansion & Parser:**
  - Robust XML reader with automatic in-memory macro expansion (`<xacro:macro>`) and mathematical expression evaluation before parsing.
  - Generates strongly typed robot AST representation via `parseUrdf()`.
- **Topological Kinematic Tree & Featherstone Algorithms:**
  - Traverses joint-link connectivity starting from the root base link.
  - Implements **Recursive Newton-Euler Algorithm (RNEA)** for inverse dynamics: calculates required joint torques $\boldsymbol{\tau}$ given joint positions $\mathbf{q}$, velocities $\dot{\mathbf{q}}$, and accelerations $\ddot{\mathbf{q}}$.
  - Implements **Articulated-Body Algorithm (ABA)** for forward dynamics: evaluates forward acceleration $\ddot{\mathbf{q}} = \mathbf{M}(\mathbf{q})^{-1} (\boldsymbol{\tau} - \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{q}, \dot{\mathbf{q}}) - \mathbf{g}(\mathbf{q}))$ in $O(N)$ operations.
- **Robotics Linters (`M7501`–`M7508`):**
  - Detects dangling parent/child link references, disconnected kinematic sub-trees, inverted joint limits (`lower > upper`), zero joint axis vectors, missing inertia tags, and non-physical inertia tensors.
- **Multi-Target Projections:**
  - **Modelica MultiBody:** Synthesizes `Modelica.Mechanics.MultiBody` robotic arms with joint friction and actuator controllers.
  - **MSC Adams:** Exports Adams `.adm` solver datasets.
  - **SIMPACK:** Generates SIMPACK `.spck` mechanisms.
  - **3D CAD:** Projects robot geometry into CSG primitives and STEP visual meshes.

---

## Command Line Interface (`msx urdf`)

```bash
msx urdf <action> [files...] [options]
```

| Action            | Description                                                                   | Key Options                                        |
| :---------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------- |
| **`lint`**        | Runs kinematic tree validation, joint limit checks, and inertia verification. | —                                                  |
| **`rnea`**        | Evaluates inverse dynamics (RNEA) at test joint coordinates.                  | `--gravity`                                        |
| **`simulate`**    | Solves articulated robot forward dynamics into time-series trajectories.      | `--stop-time`, `--step-size`, `--format=csv\|json` |
| **`to-modelica`** | Generates standard `Modelica.Mechanics.MultiBody` robot system.               | `--out=<file.mo>`                                  |
| **`to-adams`**    | Projects robot mechanism into MSC Adams `.adm` solver dataset.                | `--out=<file.adm>`                                 |
| **`to-simpack`**  | Projects robot mechanism into SIMPACK XML `.spck` model.                      | `--out=<file.spck>`                                |
| **`to-usd`**      | Projects robot into OpenUSD / UsdPhysics scene or 64-byte aligned package.    | `--usdz`, `--out=<file.usda\|file.usdz>`           |
| **`to-dae`**      | Lowers kinematic state equations directly into `DAEBuilder` arena.            | —                                                  |

### Examples

```bash
# Simulate forward dynamics under gravity to CSV/JSON trajectory
msx simulate KukaIiwa14.urdf --stop-time=2.0 --step-size=0.01 -o trajectory.csv

# Evaluate inverse dynamics (RNEA) static hold torques
msx urdf rnea KukaIiwa14.urdf

# Check for inverted joint limits or dangling parent links
msx urdf lint MobileManipulator.urdf

# Convert robot description into standard Modelica 3.x
msx urdf to-modelica PandaArm.urdf --out=PandaArm.mo

# Export to OpenUSD / UsdPhysics digital twin scene
msx urdf to-usd PandaArm.urdf --out=PandaArm.usda

# Export to 64-byte aligned USDZ package for Apple Vision Pro & NVIDIA Omniverse
msx urdf to-usd PandaArm.urdf --usdz --out=PandaArm.usdz

# Export to MSC Adams for vehicle-mounted robot simulation
msx urdf to-adams RoverArm.urdf --out=RoverArm.adm
```

---

## Interactive Ansatz Web Platform (`UrdfViewer`)

On [Ansatz](https://ansatz.social), `.urdf`, `.sdf`, and `.xacro` artifacts render directly in the interactive **Robotics Mechanism Studio**:

- **Kinematic Tree View**: High-resolution vector schematic visualizing parent/child links and joint types with pan-and-zoom controls.
- **3D Pose View**: Real-time WebGPU/Three.js multibody viewport with forward kinematics joint angle sliders ($q_i \in [q_{\text{min}}, q_{\text{max}}]$).
- **Dynamics & Linter**: Pre-flight verification results (`M7501`–`M7508`) paired with an **RNEA Gravity Hold Torques** calculator reporting static equilibrium torques ($\tau_i \text{ [N}\cdot\text{m]}$).
- **Polyglot Projections**: One-click translation to Modelica 3.x or SIMPACK JSON, with direct export to the Ansatz visual simulator.

# PLCopen XML & IEC 61131-3 Industrial Automation (`.xml`, `.st`)

`@modelscript/plcopen` (`languages/plcopen`) provides compiler, Virtual PLC cyclic execution, sampled-data DAE lowering, and formal verification for **IEC 61131-3** industrial control software and **PLCopen XML** interchange models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension          | Standard / Format               | Description                                                                    |
| :----------------- | :------------------------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.xml`, `.plcopen` | **PLCopen XML v2.01 / v2.0**    | XML exchange format for IEC 61131-3 control programs, POUs, and configurations |
| `.st`              | **IEC 61131-3 Structured Text** | Textual structured control language for PLCs and industrial controllers        |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. IEC 61131-3 Program Organization Units (POUs)

- Full support for standard control logic paradigms:
  - **Structured Text (ST)**: Variable declarations, conditionals (`IF-THEN-ELSE`), case selection, loops (`FOR`, `WHILE`), and mathematical expressions.
  - **Function Blocks (FB)**: State-retaining functional blocks including standard timers (`TON`, `TOF`, `TP`), counters (`CTU`, `CTD`, `CTUD`), and bistable multivibrators (`SR`, `RS`).
  - **Functions (FUN)**: Pure stateless mathematical computations.

### 2. High-Speed Deterministic Virtual PLC Engine

- Features a cycle-accurate Virtual PLC execution runtime (`VirtualPlc`):
  - **Sampled Scan Cycle**: Deterministic three-phase execution: input latching $\to$ logic evaluation $\to$ output write.
  - **Configurable Scan Period**: Executes discrete scan rates (e.g., $1\,\text{ms}$, $10\,\text{ms}$, $50\,\text{ms}$) coupled with continuous physical models.

### 3. Direct Sampled-Data DAE Lowering

- Compiles discrete state variables, zero-order holds (ZOH), and timer registers into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena.
- Enables closed-loop hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation of PLC control algorithms coupled with continuous Modelica physics (e.g., thermal plants, robotic actuators, motor drives).

### 4. Polyglot Projections

- **Modelica (`plcopenToModelica`)**: Lowers PLC function blocks into standard synchronous Modelica clocked state machines.
- **SysML v2 (`plcopenToSysML`)**: Maps IEC 61131-3 control architectures to SysML v2 `action def` successions and state machines.

---

## Static Analysis & Safety Linter Rules

### Diagnostics for PLCopen / IEC 61131-3 (13 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M7701` | error | `unassigned-variable-read` | Variable '<name>' is read before being assigned or initialized in POU '<pouName>'. |
| `M7702` | warning | `cyclic-task-overrun` | Computational complexity in task '<taskName>' (<stmtCount> statements) may exceed cycle time '<interval>'. |
| `M7703` | error | `recursive-pou-call` | Recursive invocation of POU '<calleeName>' detected in '<callerName>'. Recursion is prohibited in IEC 61131-3. |
| `M7704` | error | `io-mapping-collision` | Hardware I/O address collision at '<address>': multiple variables ('<var1>', '<var2>') assigned to same output. |
| `M7705` | error | `type-mismatch-assignment` | Type mismatch in assignment to '<varName>': expected '<expectedType>', got '<actualType>'. |
| `M7706` | error | `timer-preset-negative` | Timer preset time '<value>' for '<timerName>' cannot be negative. |
| `M7707` | warning | `unbounded-loop-detected` | Loop in POU '<pouName>' does not have a deterministic bounded termination condition. |
| `M7708` | error | `unknown-pou-type` | Unknown or unresolvable POU or function block type '<typeName>' instantiated in '<instanceName>'. |
| `M7709` | warning | `unreachable-code` | Unreachable code detected after '<stmtKind>' statement in POU '<pouName>'. |
| `M7710` | error | `invalid-task-interval` | Task '<taskName>' specifies invalid or non-positive periodic interval '<interval>'. |
| `M7711` | warning | `retain-without-non-volatile-storage` | Variable '<varName>' in '<pouName>' declared RETAIN but PLC configuration lacks non-volatile memory backup. |
| `M7712` | error | `division-by-zero-in-expression` | Constant expression in POU '<pouName>' evaluates to division by zero. |
| `M7713` | error | `unresolved-function-block` | Function block instance '<fbName>' in '<pouName>' does not resolve to a declared FunctionBlock. |

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Lint an IEC 61131-3 PLCopen XML project

# Lower control logic to DAE arena for closed-loop physics co-simulation

# Project into Modelica synchronous clocked state machine components

```

# IEC 62714 AutomationML & CAEX Plant Topology (`.aml`, `.caex`, `.amlx`)

`@modelscript/automationml` (`languages/automationml`) provides native WebAssembly parsing, CAEX 2.15 / 3.0 hierarchy and `InternalLink` validation, discrete-event virtual commissioning simulation, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and SSP / SysML v2 / Modelica projections for **IEC 62714 AutomationML** industrial automation and mechatronic plant engineering models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format                 | Description                                                                                                    |
| :-------- | :--------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.aml`    | IEC 62714 AutomationML | XML document combining CAEX plant topology, COLLADA 3D geometry/kinematics references, and PLCopen logic links |
| `.caex`   | IEC 62424 CAEX         | Computer Aided Engineering Exchange XML (CAEX 2.15 & 3.0)                                                      |
| `.amlx`   | AutomationML Container | Packaged AutomationML archive bundling `.aml` topologies with referenced `.dae` and `.plcxml` artifacts        |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Four-Pillar CAEX Plant Architecture

- Parses and validates all four CAEX object-oriented libraries inside `CAEXFile`:
  - **`InstanceHierarchy`**: Concrete plant cells, robots, conveyors, sensors, and PLC controllers (`InternalElement`).
  - **`SystemUnitClassLib`**: Reusable mechatronic equipment templates and vendor device catalogs.
  - **`RoleClassLib`**: Semantic engineering roles (`Resource`, `Product`, `Process`, `MechatronicAssembly`).
  - **`InterfaceClassLib`**: Typed external connectors (`ExternalInterface`: `COLLADAInterface`, `PLCopenXmlInterface`, `SignalInterface`, `Order`).

### 2. Virtual Commissioning & Scan-Cycle Simulation

- Executes deterministic discrete-time scan-cycle virtual commissioning (`runAmlVirtualCommissioning`) across linked actuators, sensors, and controller interfaces.
- Lowers continuous and discrete mechatronic state equations directly into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` linear memory arena.

### 3. Multi-Domain Projections (SSP, SysML v2, Modelica)

- **SSP 1.0 (`amlToSsp`)**: Generates `SystemStructure.ssd` co-simulation topologies from AutomationML `InstanceHierarchy` and `InternalLink` connections.
- **OMG SysML v2 (`amlToSysML2`)**: Maps `InternalElement` hierarchies and `ExternalInterface` ports to SysML v2 `part` and `port` usages.
- **Modelica 3.x (`amlToModelica`)**: Synthesizes connected acausal Modelica plant models.

---

# Adams-Compatible Multibody Dynamics

ModelScript features comprehensive, native support for **Adams-compatible** (`.adm`, `.cmd`) mechanism modeling, the classic industrial standard for mechanical systems simulation and multibody dynamics (MBD). Engineers can parse legacy Adams View command files and solver datasets, perform Grübler-Kutzbach spatial mobility analysis, evaluate 3D joint constraint residuals, and project mechanisms to modern SIMPACK and Modelica formats.

---

## Capabilities & Supported Formats

| Format                      | Extension | Description                                                                                                                                                           |
| :-------------------------- | :-------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Adams Solver Dataset**    | `.adm`    | Numerical dataset specifying rigid parts (`PART`), marker frames (`MARKER`), kinematic joints (`JOINT`), force elements (`SPRINGDAMPER`, `BUSHING`), and constraints. |
| **Adams View Command File** | `.cmd`    | Interactive parametric command scripts defining mechanism geometry, design variables, and simulation runs.                                                            |

### Key Architectural Features

- **Lexer & Parser:**
  - Robust deck ingestion supporting scientific notation (`1.5D-03`), inline comments (`!`), line continuations (`...`), and block cards.
  - Lossless serialization back to standardized `.adm` solver format via `serializeAdams()`.
- **Spatial 3D Kinematics:**
  - Full evaluation of Euler 3-1-3 and Tait-Bryan 1-2-3 rotation matrices.
  - Analytical joint constraint formulation for standard spatial joint primitives (Revolute, Spherical, Prismatic, Cylindrical, Planar, Universal).
- **Grübler-Kutzbach Mobility Analysis:**
  - Calculates mechanism degrees of freedom ($M = 6(n - 1) - \sum c_i$).
  - Identifies redundant kinematic constraints and overconstrained multi-loop linkages.
- **Multibody Linters (`M7301`–`M7310`):**
  - Flags missing ground parts, dangling marker references, unphysical inertia tensors violating the triangle inequality ($I_{xx} + I_{yy} \ge I_{zz}$), massless moving parts, and negative spring/damping parameters.
- **Cross-Domain Projections:**
  - **SIMPACK MBD:** Maps parts, markers, and spatial joints to SIMPACK `.spck` XML models.
  - **Modelica MultiBody:** Synthesizes standard `Modelica.Mechanics.MultiBody` parts and joint components.

---

## Command Line Interface (`msx adams`)

```bash
msx adams <action> [files...] [options]
```

| Action            | Description                                                                    | Key Options                                                     |
| :---------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **`lint`**        | Runs structural validation, inertia verification, and kinematic sanity checks. | —                                                               |
| **`mobility`**    | Evaluates spatial degrees of freedom and overconstrained loops.                | —                                                               |
| **`to-simpack`**  | Projects Adams mechanism to SIMPACK XML (`.spck`).                             | `--out=<file.spck>`                                             |
| **`to-modelica`** | Projects Adams mechanism to `Modelica.Mechanics.MultiBody`.                    | `--out=<file.mo>`                                               |
| **`simulate`**    | Lowers to a DAE and integrates it in time.                                     | `--stop-time`, `--step`, `--stabilization=baumgarte\|algebraic` |

### Examples

```bash
# Calculate mechanism spatial degrees of freedom
msx adams mobility FourBarLinkage.adm

# Validate inertia tensors and marker references
msx adams lint LandingGear.adm

# Convert Adams dataset into SIMPACK XML format
msx adams to-simpack RobotArm.adm --out=RobotArm.spck

# Compute mechanism mobility (degrees of freedom)
msx adams mobility ExcavatorMechanism.adm
```

# EnergyPlus Building Simulation (`.idf`, `.epjson`)

`@modelscript/energyplus` (`languages/energyplus`) provides compiler, thermal lumped-capacitance DAE lowering, and bidirectional TGG synchronization for **US Department of Energy (DOE) EnergyPlus** building energy and HVAC models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format                     | Description                                                          |
| :-------- | :------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.idf`    | EnergyPlus Input Data File | Industry-standard comma/semicolon delimited building simulation deck |
| `.epjson` | EnergyPlus JSON Schema     | Structured JSON schema representation of EnergyPlus models           |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Lumped-Capacitance Multi-Zone Thermal DAEs

- Translates architectural thermal zones and building envelopes into continuous energy balance DAEs, where the rate of change of zone air thermal energy equals the sum of conductive, convective, solar, internal, and HVAC heat transfer rates:
  $$C_{z,i} \frac{dT_{z,i}}{dt} = \sum_{j} \dot{Q}_{\text{cond},ij} + \sum_{k} \dot{Q}_{\text{conv},ik} + \dot{Q}_{\text{solar}} + \dot{Q}_{\text{internal}} + \dot{Q}_{\text{HVAC}}$$

  | Symbol                      | Meaning                                                       | Units / Domain                       |
  | :-------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ | :----------------------------------- |
  | $C_{z,i}$                   | Effective thermal capacitance of thermal zone $i$             | $\text{J}\cdot\text{K}^{-1}$ ($> 0$) |
  | $T_{z,i}$                   | Dry-bulb air temperature of zone $i$                          | $\text{K}$ (or $^\circ\text{C}$)     |
  | $t$                         | Simulation time                                               | $\text{s}$                           |
  | $\dot{Q}_{\text{cond},ij}$  | Conductive heat transfer rate from adjacent zone/surface $j$  | $\text{W}$                           |
  | $\dot{Q}_{\text{conv},ik}$  | Convective heat transfer rate from interior surface $k$       | $\text{W}$                           |
  | $\dot{Q}_{\text{solar}}$    | Transmitted solar radiation heat gain                         | $\text{W}$ ($\ge 0$)                 |
  | $\dot{Q}_{\text{internal}}$ | Internal sensible heat gains (lighting, occupants, equipment) | $\text{W}$ ($\ge 0$)                 |
  | $\dot{Q}_{\text{HVAC}}$     | Net heating or cooling rate supplied by the HVAC system       | $\text{W}$                           |

- **Envelope Conduction**: Multi-layer wall, floor, and roof constructions with layer-resolved thermal conductivity $k$, density $\rho$, and specific heat $c_p$.
- **Window & Fenestration Optics**: U-factor, Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (SHGC), and visible transmittance shading calculations.
- **Internal Loads**: Schedules for lighting, occupancy sensible/latent heat release, and plug-load equipment dissipation.

### 2. Direct DAE Lowering

- Compiles building geometry and HVAC schedules directly into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` linear memory arena, enabling co-simulation with dynamic grid power models ([`@modelscript/pscad`](./pscad.md)) and district energy networks.

### 3. Bidirectional Triple Graph Grammar (TGG) Sync

- Implements bidirectional TGG rules (`energyplus-sync.ts`) synchronizing EnergyPlus thermal zones with:
  - **Modelica (`Modelica.Thermal` / IBPSA Buildings)**: Automatic translation into acausal thermal components and fluid loops.
  - **STEP CAD (ISO 10303)**: Validates physical geometric volume and boundary surface areas against 3D architectural CAD envelopes.

---

## Verification, Maturity & Benchmarks

Tier: `alpha` | Pass Rate: 100% (2/2) | Parse Latency: 0.09 ms (p95: 0.11 ms)

| Benchmark Case | Scale | Reference Oracle | Metric / Threshold | Measured | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: |
| Canonical Fixture Parse | micro | ModelScript WASM GLR | `ast-pass-rate <= 1` | `0` | PASS |
| Multi-Zone 3R2C Building Thermal Model to DAEBuilder | standard | DOE EnergyPlus / 3R2C Multi-Zone Thermal DAE | `dae-parity <= 0` | `0` | PASS |

| `M7902` | warning | `non-convex-surface-polygon` | Surface polygon '<surfName>' in zone '<zoneName>' violates planar convexity, which may impair solar raytracing and view factor calculations. |

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Lint an EnergyPlus building model deck
msx energyplus lint CommercialOffice.idf

# Lower thermal zones to ModelScript linear memory DAE arena
msx energyplus to-dae CommercialOffice.idf --out=office.dae.json

# Project into standard Modelica IBPSA Buildings library components
msx energyplus to-modelica CommercialOffice.idf -o BuildingThermalModel.mo
```

# EPANET Water Distribution Networks (`.inp`)

`@modelscript/epanet` (`languages/epanet`) provides native parsing, hydraulic simulation, DAE lowering, and formal verification for **US EPA EPANET** pressurized drinking water distribution networks and municipal water infrastructure.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format            | Description                                                                       |
| :-------- | :---------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.inp`    | EPANET Input File | Industry-standard network topology, pipes, pumps, valves, and water quality decks |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Todini Global Gradient Method (GGM) Hydraulic Solver

- Implements the Todini Global Gradient Algorithm (`todini-ggm.ts`) for quadratic/nonlinear pipe network equilibrium:
  - **Conservation of Mass at Junctions** (total inflow minus total outflow equals external nodal demand):
    $$\sum_{k \in \text{in}(i)} Q_k - \sum_{k \in \text{out}(i)} Q_k = D_i$$
  - **Conservation of Energy across Pipe Loops** (hydraulic head drop between nodes equals frictional head loss):
    $$h_i - h_j = h_{L,ij} = r Q_{ij} |Q_{ij}|^{\alpha - 1}$$

  | Symbol        | Meaning                                                                      | Units / Domain                                                                 |
  | :------------ | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | $Q_k, Q_{ij}$ | Volumetric flow rate in pipe $k$ or from node $i$ to node $j$                | $\text{m}^3\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ (or $\text{L}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$, $\text{gpm}$) |
  | $D_i$         | External nodal water demand at junction $i$                                  | $\text{m}^3\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ (or $\text{L}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$, $\text{gpm}$) |
  | $h_i, h_j$    | Hydraulic grade line (piezometric head) at nodes $i$ and $j$                 | $\text{m}$ (or $\text{ft}$)                                                    |
  | $h_{L,ij}$    | Frictional head loss along pipe $(i, j)$                                     | $\text{m}$ (or $\text{ft}$)                                                    |
  | $r$           | Pipe hydraulic resistance coefficient (from length, diameter, roughness)     | $\text{s}^{\alpha}\cdot\text{m}^{1-3\alpha}$ ($> 0$)                           |
  | $\alpha$      | Flow exponent ($1.852$ Hazen-Williams, $2.0$ Darcy-Weisbach / Chezy-Manning) | Dimensionless ($> 0$)                                                          |

- Supports **Hazen-Williams**, **Darcy-Weisbach**, and **Chezy-Manning** head loss friction models.

### 2. Multi-Component Hydraulic Elements

- **Pumps**: Head gain curves modeled via 3-point polynomial and power-law relationships ($h_p = h_0 - a Q^b$).
- **Tanks & Reservoirs**: Dynamic elevated storage tanks with hydrostatic pressure differential equations, where the water level rises or falls in proportion to net volumetric inflow divided by tank cross-sectional area:
  $$A_{\text{tank}} \frac{dh}{dt} = \sum Q_{\text{in}} - \sum Q_{\text{out}}$$
  where $A_{\text{tank}}$ is the tank cross-sectional area ($\text{m}^2$, $> 0$), $h$ is the water surface elevation ($\text{m}$), $t$ is time ($\text{s}$), and $Q_{\text{in}}, Q_{\text{out}}$ are incoming and outgoing pipe volumetric flow rates ($\text{m}^3\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$).
- **Control Valves**: Pressure Reducing Valves (PRV), Pressure Sustaining Valves (PSV), and Flow Control Valves (FCV).

### 3. Extended-Period, Pressure-Driven, MOC Water Hammer, Quality & AWWA M36

- **Extended Period Simulation (`eps`) & Optimal Pump Scheduling (`ops`)**: Simulates 24–168 hour diurnal demand patterns and tank storage cycles while optimizing pump energy against time-of-use electricity tariffs.
- **Wagner Pressure-Driven Demand (`pdd`) & Fire Flow**: Evaluates pressure-deficient delivery ($Q_i = D_i \sqrt{(P_i - P_{\min}) / (P_{\text{req}} - P_{\min})}$) and ISO hydrant residual pressure limits ($\ge 20\text{ psi}$).
- **Method of Characteristics (MOC) Water Hammer (`surge`)**: Solves 1D elastic Joukowsky wave propagation ($\Delta H = \pm \frac{a}{g} \Delta V$) for rapid valve closure and pump trip transients.
- **Advective Water Quality (`quality`), AWWA M36 Water Audit (`audit`), GIS Ingestion (`from-gis`) & EPA LCRR**: Models chlorine decay and water age, computes Infrastructure Leakage Index (ILI), ingests GeoJSON pipe/node layers, and exports US EPA Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR) inventories.

### 4. Direct DAE Lowering & Modelica Projection

- Compiles the entire municipal pipe and tank network into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` SoA linear memory arena.
- Projects EPANET networks into standard `Modelica.Fluid` pipes, reservoirs, and centrifugal pumps for joint thermo-fluid studies.

---

| `M8101` | error | `isolated-hydraulic-node` | Hydraulic node '<nodeId>' is isolated with no connecting pipes or pumps. |

| `M8103` | error | `non-monotonic-pump-curve` | Pump head curve '<curveId>' violates decreasing monotonicity: head increases from <value> to <value> between flow <value> and <value>. |

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Inspect and lint an EPANET municipal water network
msx epanet inspect MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp
msx epanet lint MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp

# Solve steady-state network hydraulics (Todini GGM), EPS, PDD, and MOC water hammer
msx epanet solve MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp
msx epanet eps MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp
msx epanet pdd MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp
msx epanet surge MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp

# Run AWWA M36 IWA water audit, optimal pump scheduling, water quality, and topological diff
msx epanet audit MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp
msx epanet ops MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp
msx epanet quality MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp
msx epanet diff Baseline.inp Proposed.inp

# Ingest GeoJSON GIS pipe and node layers into an EPANET .inp deck
msx epanet from-gis pipes.geojson --nodes=junctions.geojson --out=MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp

# Lower network dynamics into ModelScript linear DAE arena or Modelica.Fluid
msx epanet to-dae MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp --out=network.dae.json
msx epanet to-modelica MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp -o MunicipalPipes.mo
```

# EPA SWMM Stormwater & Urban Hydrology (`.inp`)

`@modelscript/swmm` (`languages/swmm`) provides zero-regex parsing, 1D Saint-Venant dynamic wave hydraulic routing, DAE lowering, and Modelica 3.x projection for **US EPA Stormwater Management Model (SWMM 5.x)** urban drainage, sewer collection, and flood mitigation networks.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format              | Description                                                                                                      |
| :-------- | :------------------ | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.inp`    | EPA SWMM Input File | Industry-standard stormwater network deck (junctions, conduits, outfalls, subcatchments, pumps, weirs, orifices) |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. 1D Saint-Venant Dynamic Wave Routing

- Models open-channel and pressurized sewer hydraulics via the one-dimensional **Saint-Venant equations of unsteady flow**:
  - **Conservation of Mass (Continuity)** (balances local cross-sectional storage change and axial discharge gradient against lateral inflow):
    $$\frac{\partial A}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = q_{\text{lateral}}$$
  - **Conservation of Momentum** (balances fluid acceleration and convective momentum flux against pressure/gravity head gradients and frictional resistance):
    $$\frac{\partial Q}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( \frac{Q^2}{A} \right) + g A \frac{\partial H}{\partial x} + g A S_f = 0$$
- Uses **Manning's open-channel equation** to relate discharge to friction slope $S_f$ via conduit roughness and hydraulic radius:
  $$Q = \frac{k_m}{n} A R_h^{2/3} S_f^{1/2} \quad \implies \quad S_f = \frac{n^2 Q |Q|}{k_m^2 A^2 R_h^{4/3}}$$

  | Symbol               | Meaning                                                 | Units / Domain                                            |
  | :------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------ | :-------------------------------------------------------- |
  | $t, x$               | Time and longitudinal distance along conduit            | $\text{s}$, $\text{m}$                                    |
  | $A$                  | Wetted cross-sectional flow area                        | $\text{m}^2$, $> 0$                                       |
  | $Q$                  | Volumetric flow rate (discharge)                        | $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$                                     |
  | $q_{\text{lateral}}$ | Lateral inflow per unit conduit length                  | $\text{m}^2/\text{s}$                                     |
  | $g$                  | Gravitational acceleration ($9.81\text{ m/s}^2$)        | $\text{m/s}^2$                                            |
  | $H$                  | Hydraulic head ($z + d$, invert elevation plus depth)   | $\text{m}$                                                |
  | $S_f$                | Friction slope (energy grade line slope)                | dimensionless                                             |
  | $n$                  | Manning roughness coefficient                           | $\text{s/m}^{1/3}$ (or US equiv.), $> 0$                  |
  | $k_m$                | Unit conversion factor ($1.0$ SI, $1.486$ US customary) | $\text{m}^{1/3}/\text{s}$ (or $\text{ft}^{1/3}/\text{s}$) |
  | $R_h$                | Hydraulic radius ($A / P_{\text{wetted}}$)              | $\text{m}$, $> 0$                                         |

### 2. Node & Link Hydraulic Structures

- **Junctions & Storage Units**: Enforces continuous water-surface elevation mass conservation at each node by balancing net link inflows, external runoff/dry-weather inflows, and surface flooding losses:
  $$A_{\text{node}} \frac{dH_i}{dt} = \sum Q_{\text{in}} - \sum Q_{\text{out}} + Q_{\text{inflow}} - Q_{\text{flood}}$$

  | Symbol                          | Meaning                                              | Units / Domain                 |
  | :------------------------------ | :--------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------- |
  | $A_{\text{node}}$               | Effective nodal surface plan area                    | $\text{m}^2$, $> 0$            |
  | $H_i$                           | Hydraulic head (water surface elevation) at node $i$ | $\text{m}$                     |
  | $Q_{\text{in}}, Q_{\text{out}}$ | Incoming and outgoing conduit/regulator flows        | $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$, $\ge 0$ |
  | $Q_{\text{inflow}}$             | External subcatchment runoff and dry-weather inflow  | $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$, $\ge 0$ |
  | $Q_{\text{flood}}$              | Surface ponding or street flooding overflow rate     | $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$, $\ge 0$ |

- **Conduits**: Circular, rectangular, trapezoidal, and irregular natural river cross-sections with entrance/exit minor head loss coefficients.
- **Outfalls**: Free, normal, tidal, and fixed water elevation boundary conditions.
- **Regulators**: Orifices, transverse/side-flow weirs, and variable-speed lift pumps.

### 3. Direct DAE Lowering

- Compiles the entire stormwater collection network into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` struct-of-arrays linear memory arena.
- Enables co-simulation of municipal drinking water networks ([`@modelscript/epanet`](./epanet.md)) and drainage networks within the same computational arena.

### 4. Real-Time Control (RTC), Pollutant Washoff, GIS Ingestion & EPA NetDMR

- **Real-Time Control (`rtc`) & Pollutant Washoff (`quality`)**: Simulates dynamic weir/orifice/pump PID and rule-based flood gates alongside exponential land-use pollutant buildup and runoff washoff (TSS, TP, TN).
- **GIS Ingestion (`from-gis`), Network Diff (`diff`) & EPA NetDMR Export**: Ingests GeoJSON conduits, manholes, and subcatchments (`gis-ingestor.ts`), computes topological stormwater diffs, and exports US EPA NPDES NetDMR CSO/SSO overflow monitoring tables (`netdmr-exporter.ts`).

### 5. Bidirectional Modelica 3.x Projection

- Projects SWMM nodes and channels into `Modelica.Fluid` open-channel tanks, flow conduits, and boundary reservoirs.

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

The SWMM linter verifies network graph integrity and hydraulic feasibility before simulation:

### Diagnostics for EPA SWMM (13 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M8201` | error | `dangling-node-reference` | Link '<linkId>' references undefined <role> node '<nodeId>'. |
| `M8202` | warning | `adverse-conduit-slope` | Conduit '<conduitId>' has adverse slope: inlet elevation (<value>) is lower than outlet elevation (<value>). |
| `M8203` | error | `missing-cross-section` | Conduit '<conduitId>' has no hydraulic cross-section definition in '[XSECTIONS]'. |
| `M8204` | error | `unsupported-outfall-type` | Outfall '<outfallId>' specifies unsupported boundary condition type '<type>'. |
| `M8205` | warning | `surcharge-overflow-risk` | Junction '<junctionId>' rim elevation (<value>) is lower than connected conduit crown (<value>), creating surcharge overflow risk. |
| `M8206` | error | `duplicate-node-id` | Duplicate node identifier '<nodeId>' declared in network. |
| `M8207` | error | `duplicate-link-id` | Duplicate link identifier '<linkId>' declared in network. |
| `M8208` | error | `negative-roughness` | Conduit '<conduitId>' specifies non-positive Manning's roughness coefficient (n = <n>). |
| `M8209` | error | `zero-length-conduit` | Conduit '<conduitId>' specifies non-positive length (<len>). |

| `M8211` | error | `subcatchment-outlet-not-found` | Subcatchment '<subId>' references non-existent discharge outlet '<outletId>'. |
| `M8212` | error | `weir-offset-negative` | Weir '<weirId>' specifies negative crest height offset (<offset>). |
| `M8213` | error | `invalid-discharge-coefficient` | Link '<linkId>' specifies non-positive discharge coefficient (Cd = <cd>). |

# USACE HEC-RAS River Hydraulics (`.g01`, `.g02`, `.rasgeo`)

`@modelscript/hec-ras` (`languages/hec-ras`) provides native parsing, 1D steady backwater profile solution, dynamic wave Saint-Venant DAE lowering, and cross-section validation for **US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) HEC-RAS** river geometries and steady/unsteady flow decks.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension              | Format                        | Description                                                                                   |
| :--------------------- | :---------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.g01`, `.g02`, `.g03` | HEC-RAS Geometry File         | River reach coordinates, cross-section station-elevations, Manning's $n$, and weir structures |
| `.rasgeo`, `.geo`      | Modern HEC-RAS ASCII Geometry | Unified multi-reach geometry exchange format                                                  |
| `.f01`, `.f02`         | HEC-RAS Steady Flow File      | Boundary conditions (known WS, critical depth, normal depth, rating curves)                   |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Standard Step Method 1D Backwater Solver

- Solves the steady-state 1D energy conservation equation between adjacent cross-sections (upstream section 2 and downstream section 1), balancing water surface elevation plus velocity head:
  $$WSE_2 + \alpha_2 \frac{V_2^2}{2g} = WSE_1 + \alpha_1 \frac{V_1^2}{2g} + h_e$$
  where the head loss $h_e$ incorporates reach friction loss and expansion/contraction eddy losses:
  $$h_e = L \bar{S}_f + C \left| \alpha_2 \frac{V_2^2}{2g} - \alpha_1 \frac{V_1^2}{2g} \right|$$
- Friction slope is evaluated via Manning's conveyance formula across subdivided overbank and main-channel zones:
  $$\bar{S}_f = \left( \frac{Q}{\sum K_i} \right)^2, \quad K_i = \frac{1}{n_i} A_i R_i^{2/3}$$

  | Symbol               | Meaning                                                              | Units / Domain                                                  |
  | :------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | $WSE_1, WSE_2$       | Water surface elevation at cross-sections 1 and 2                    | $\text{m}$ (or $\text{ft}$)                                     |
  | $V_1, V_2$           | Average cross-sectional flow velocities                              | $\text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ (or $\text{ft}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$) |
  | $\alpha_1, \alpha_2$ | Velocity weighting (Coriolis) coefficients                           | Dimensionless ($\ge 1$)                                         |
  | $g$                  | Gravitational acceleration                                           | $\text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$ (or $\text{ft}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$) |
  | $h_e$                | Total energy head loss between cross-sections 2 and 1                | $\text{m}$ (or $\text{ft}$), $\ge 0$                            |
  | $L$                  | Discharge-weighted reach length                                      | $\text{m}$ (or $\text{ft}$), $> 0$                              |
  | $\bar{S}_f$          | Representative friction slope between sections                       | Dimensionless ($\text{m}/\text{m}$, $\ge 0$)                    |
  | $C$                  | Expansion or contraction loss coefficient                            | Dimensionless ($\in [0, 1]$)                                    |
  | $Q$                  | Total volumetric river discharge                                     | $\text{m}^3\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ (or $\text{cfs}$)                |
  | $K_i$                | Hydraulic conveyance of subsection $i$ (LOB, channel, ROB)           | $\text{m}^3\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$                                  |
  | $n_i, A_i, R_i$      | Manning roughness, flow area, and hydraulic radius of subsection $i$ | $\text{s}\cdot\text{m}^{-1/3}$, $\text{m}^2$, $\text{m}$        |

- Supports subcritical, supercritical, and mixed flow regimes with hydraulic jump detection.

### 2. Multi-Zone Cross-Section Hydrodynamics

- Segmented cross-sections with distinct left overbank (LOB), main channel, and right overbank (ROB) roughness coefficients.
- Automated wetted perimeter $P(y)$, flow area $A(y)$, and hydraulic radius $R_h(y)$ quadrature across irregular surveyed station-elevation slices.
- Inline structures: broad-crested and ogee weirs with standard discharge coefficient formulations ($Q = C_d L H^{3/2}$).

### 3. Zero-GC Saint-Venant DAE Lowering

- Lowers the unsteady 1D shallow water (Saint-Venant) conservation of mass and momentum equations into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` linear memory arena:
  $$\frac{\partial A}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = q_L$$
  $$\frac{\partial Q}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\frac{\beta Q^2}{A}\right) + g A \frac{\partial h}{\partial x} + g A (S_f - S_0) = 0$$

  | Symbol     | Meaning                                      | Units / Domain                      |
  | :--------- | :------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------- |
  | $A$        | Cross-sectional wetted flow area             | $\text{m}^2$ ($> 0$)                |
  | $Q$        | Volumetric discharge along the channel       | $\text{m}^3\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$      |
  | $t, x$     | Time and longitudinal channel coordinate     | $\text{s}$, $\text{m}$              |
  | $q_L$      | Lateral inflow per unit channel length       | $\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$      |
  | $\beta$    | Momentum correction (Boussinesq) coefficient | Dimensionless ($\ge 1$)             |
  | $h$        | Water depth (or stage)                       | $\text{m}$ ($> 0$)                  |
  | $S_f, S_0$ | Friction slope and channel bed slope         | Dimensionless ($\text{m}/\text{m}$) |

- Enables direct co-simulation with urban drainage (`@modelscript/swmm`), drinking water networks (`@modelscript/epanet`), and regional aquifers (`@modelscript/modflow`).

---

## Verification, Maturity & Benchmarks

Tier: `alpha` | Pass Rate: 100% (2/2) | Parse Latency: 0.53 ms (p95: 1.13 ms)

| Benchmark Case | Scale | Reference Oracle | Metric / Threshold | Measured | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: |
| Canonical Fixture Parse | micro | ModelScript Native Parser | `ast-pass-rate <= 1` | `0` | PASS |
| Bald Eagle Creek 1D Subcritical Backwater Profile | standard | USACE HEC-RAS 6.x | `dae-parity <= 0.001` | `0` | PASS |

Reproduce: `npm run bench:languages -- --lang=hec-ras`

---

## Static Analysis & Pre-Flight Linter Rules

### Diagnostics for USACE HEC-RAS (8 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M1001` | error | `hecras-parse-error` | Syntax error in HEC-RAS deck: <err>. |
| `M2001` | error | `hecras-reach-not-found` | River '<river>', reach '<reach>' was referenced but not defined in geometry. |
| `M3001` | error | `hecras-station-inversion` | Cross-section at station '<station>' has inverted station offsets: <currSta> <= <prevSta>. Offsets must be strictly monotonically increasing. |
| `M3002` | warning | `hecras-manning-out-of-bounds` | Manning roughness coefficient <n> at station '<station>' is outside typical physical bounds (0.01 - 0.20). |
| `M3003` | error | `hecras-bank-station-out-of-bounds` | Bank station <bank> at station '<station>' is outside cross-section limits [<minSta>, <maxSta>]. |
| `M4001` | error | `hecras-disconnected-reach` | River reach '<river>, <reach>' has fewer than 2 cross-sections and cannot form a valid conveyance profile. |
| `M5001` | warning | `hecras-adverse-slope` | Adverse bed slope detected between upstream station '<usStation>' (invert <usBed> m) and downstream station '<dsStation>' (invert <dsBed> m). |
| `M5002` | error | `hecras-missing-downstream-boundary` | Reach '<river>, <reach>' is missing a downstream boundary condition (Normal Depth, Known WS, or Rating Curve). |

# USGS MODFLOW 6 Groundwater Aquifers (`.dis`, `.dis6`, `.npf`, `.wel`)

`@modelscript/modflow` (`languages/modflow`) provides native structured block parsing, 3D Darcy cell conductance evaluation, aquifer mass balance solution, and DAE lowering for **US Geological Survey (USGS) MODFLOW 6** regional groundwater flow models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension       | Format                         | Description                                                                            |
| :-------------- | :----------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.dis`, `.dis6` | MODFLOW Discretization Package | 3D layered regular grid dimensions ($\Delta r, \Delta c$, top, bottom elevations)      |
| `.npf`          | Node Property Flow Package     | Horizontal/vertical hydraulic conductivities ($K_{xx}, K_{33}$) and storage properties |
| `.wel`          | Well Package                   | Extraction and injection well pumping rates per grid cell                              |
| `.riv`          | River Package                  | Surface water-groundwater hydraulic exchange conductance and river stage               |
| `.chd`          | Constant-Head Package          | Fixed piezometric head boundary conditions                                             |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. 3D Darcy Inter-Cell Hydraulic Conductance

- Calculates harmonic-mean directional hydraulic conductances between adjacent grid cells $(i, j)$ and enforces steady-state groundwater mass conservation at each cell:
  $$C_{ij} = \frac{2 K_i K_j}{K_i \Delta x_j + K_j \Delta x_i} \cdot A_{ij}$$
  $$\sum_{j \in \text{neighbors}(i)} C_{ij} (h_j - h_i) + Q_{\text{wel}, i} + Q_{\text{riv}, i} + Q_{\text{chd}, i} = 0$$

  | Symbol                                                    | Meaning                                                                                    | Units / Domain        |
  | :-------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------- |
  | $C_{ij}$                                                  | Inter-cell hydraulic conductance between cells $i$ and $j$                                 | $\text{m}^2/\text{d}$ |
  | $K_i, K_j$                                                | Directional hydraulic conductivities of cells $i$ and $j$                                  | $\text{m/d}$          |
  | $\Delta x_i, \Delta x_j$                                  | Cell dimensions along the flow direction                                                   | $\text{m}$            |
  | $A_{ij}$                                                  | Shared cross-sectional interface area between cells $i$ and $j$                            | $\text{m}^2$          |
  | $h_i, h_j$                                                | Hydraulic (piezometric) heads in cells $i$ and $j$                                         | $\text{m}$            |
  | $Q_{\text{wel}, i}, Q_{\text{riv}, i}, Q_{\text{chd}, i}$ | Volumetric source/sink fluxes at cell $i$ from wells, rivers, and constant-head boundaries | $\text{m}^3/\text{d}$ |

### 2. Riverbed Seepage & Groundwater Interaction

- Simulates bidirectional surface-groundwater exchange flux driven by the head difference between the river stage and either the aquifer cell head (connected) or the riverbed bottom elevation (perched/disconnected):
  $$Q_{\text{riv}} = \begin{cases} C_{\text{riv}} (h_{\text{stage}} - h_{\text{cell}}), & h_{\text{cell}} > z_{\text{rbot}} \\ C_{\text{riv}} (h_{\text{stage}} - z_{\text{rbot}}), & h_{\text{cell}} \le z_{\text{rbot}} \end{cases}$$

  | Symbol             | Meaning                                                                     | Units / Domain        |
  | :----------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------- |
  | $Q_{\text{riv}}$   | Volumetric seepage flux from river into aquifer cell ($>0$ gaining aquifer) | $\text{m}^3/\text{d}$ |
  | $C_{\text{riv}}$   | Riverbed hydraulic conductance                                              | $\text{m}^2/\text{d}$ |
  | $h_{\text{stage}}$ | River water surface elevation (stage)                                       | $\text{m}$            |
  | $h_{\text{cell}}$  | Groundwater head in the underlying aquifer cell                             | $\text{m}$            |
  | $z_{\text{rbot}}$  | Elevation of the bottom of the riverbed sediment layer                      | $\text{m}$            |

- Coupled directly to river hydraulics (`@modelscript/hec-ras`) and urban stormwater runoff (`@modelscript/swmm`).

### 3. DAE Formulation for Aquifer Storage Dynamics

- Lowers unconfined/confined transient head equations into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder`, equating elastic storage change to net cell inflow:
  $$S_s \Delta V \frac{dh}{dt} = \sum Q_{\text{flux}}$$

  | Symbol                 | Meaning                                                                | Units / Domain         |
  | :--------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------- |
  | $S_s$                  | Specific storage of the porous medium                                  | $\text{m}^{-1}$        |
  | $\Delta V$             | Cell bulk volume                                                       | $\text{m}^3$           |
  | $h, t$                 | Hydraulic head and time                                                | $\text{m}$, $\text{d}$ |
  | $\sum Q_{\text{flux}}$ | Net sum of all inter-cell and boundary volumetric fluxes into the cell | $\text{m}^3/\text{d}$  |

- Allows municipal water planners to evaluate sustained well yield against drinking water demand profiles (`@modelscript/epanet`).

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M1001` | error | `modflow-parse-error` | Syntax or structure error in MODFLOW deck: <err>. |

| `M3001` | error | `modflow-invalid-conductivity` | Hydraulic conductivity K = <k> is invalid. K must be strictly positive (K > 0). |

```bash
# Inspect and summarize MODFLOW 6 grid discretization, conductivity, and boundary packages

```

# EPA LandGEM Biogas & Landfill Gas (`.landgem`, `.lfg`, `.biogas`)

`@modelscript/landgem` (`languages/landgem`) provides native parsing, first-order methane decay kinetics, continuous stirred-tank anaerobic digestion (ADM1), and Combined Heat & Power (CHP) DAE lowering for **US EPA LandGEM** and industrial organic waste-to-energy models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension          | Format                      | Description                                                                        |
| :----------------- | :-------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.landgem`, `.lfg` | EPA LandGEM Model           | Annual solid waste acceptance cohorts, methane capacity $L_0$, and decay rates $k$ |
| `.biogas`          | Biogas / ADM1 Digester Deck | CSTR reactor parameters, hydraulic retention times (HRT), and influent COD loads   |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. First-Order Decay Methane Generation Kinetics

- Evaluates the canonical US EPA LandGEM equation, which sums the exponentially decaying methane generation contributions across all historical annual waste cohorts $i$:
  $$Q_{\text{CH}_4}(t) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} 2 k L_0 M_i e^{-k t_{i}}$$

  | Symbol               | Meaning                                               | Units / Domain                             |
  | :------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------- |
  | $Q_{\text{CH}_4}(t)$ | Methane generation rate at time $t$                   | $\text{m}^3/\text{yr}$                     |
  | $t$                  | Simulation time                                       | $\text{yr}$                                |
  | $i, n$               | Waste cohort index and total number of annual cohorts | $\text{dimensionless}$ ($i = 1, \dots, n$) |
  | $k$                  | Methane generation rate constant                      | $\text{yr}^{-1}$                           |
  | $L_0$                | Potential methane generation capacity                 | $\text{m}^3/\text{Mg}$                     |
  | $M_i$                | Mass of waste accepted in year $i$                    | $\text{Mg}$                                |
  | $t_i$                | Age of waste cohort $i$ at time $t$                   | $\text{yr}$ ($t_i \ge 0$)                  |

- Evaluates landfill gas (LFG) collection efficiency and non-methane organic compound (NMOC) emissions.

### 2. ADM1 Continuous Anaerobic Digestion Engine

- Models mesophilic ($37^\circ\text{C}$) and thermophilic ($55^\circ\text{C}$) anaerobic CSTR digesters by computing the volumetric chemical oxygen demand (COD) removal rate and scaling it by reactor volume and methane yield:
  $$r_{\text{COD}} = \eta_{\text{removal}} \cdot \frac{S_{\text{COD,in}}}{HRT}$$
  $$Q_{\text{CH}_4,\text{dig}} = r_{\text{COD}} \cdot V_{\text{reactor}} \cdot Y_{\text{CH}_4/\text{COD}}$$

  | Symbol                       | Meaning                                                                | Units / Domain                                               |
  | :--------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------- |
  | $r_{\text{COD}}$             | Volumetric COD removal rate                                            | $\text{kg COD}/(\text{m}^3 \cdot \text{d})$                  |
  | $\eta_{\text{removal}}$      | Fractional COD removal efficiency                                      | $\text{dimensionless}$ ($0 \le \eta_{\text{removal}} \le 1$) |
  | $S_{\text{COD,in}}$          | Influent COD concentration                                             | $\text{kg COD}/\text{m}^3$                                   |
  | $HRT$                        | Hydraulic retention time                                               | $\text{d}$ ($HRT > 0$)                                       |
  | $Q_{\text{CH}_4,\text{dig}}$ | Digester methane production rate                                       | $\text{m}^3\,\text{CH}_4/\text{d}$                           |
  | $V_{\text{reactor}}$         | Active liquid volume of the CSTR digester                              | $\text{m}^3$                                                 |
  | $Y_{\text{CH}_4/\text{COD}}$ | Theoretical methane yield per unit COD removed ($\approx 0.35$ at STP) | $\text{m}^3\,\text{CH}_4/\text{kg COD}_{\text{removed}}$     |

- Monitors Volatile Fatty Acid (VFA) accumulation and digester souring risk based on pH.

### 3. Combined Heat & Power (CHP) DAE Lowering

- Couples biogas production directly into electrical and thermal power output equations in `DAEBuilder` using the fuel's lower heating value and conversion efficiencies:
  $$P_{\text{elec}}(t) = Q_{\text{CH}_4}(t) \cdot \text{LHV}_{\text{CH}_4} \cdot \eta_{\text{elec}}$$
  $$P_{\text{thermal}}(t) = Q_{\text{CH}_4}(t) \cdot \text{LHV}_{\text{CH}_4} \cdot \eta_{\text{thermal}}$$

  | Symbol                     | Meaning                                  | Units / Domain                                               |
  | :------------------------- | :--------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------- |
  | $P_{\text{elec}}(t)$       | Net electrical power output              | $\text{W}$ (or $\text{kW}$)                                  |
  | $P_{\text{thermal}}(t)$    | Recoverable thermal power output         | $\text{W}$ (or $\text{kW}$)                                  |
  | $Q_{\text{CH}_4}(t)$       | Methane volumetric flow rate at time $t$ | $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$                                        |
  | $\text{LHV}_{\text{CH}_4}$ | Lower heating value of methane           | $\text{J}/\text{m}^3$                                        |
  | $\eta_{\text{elec}}$       | Electrical conversion efficiency         | $\text{dimensionless}$ ($0 \le \eta_{\text{elec}} \le 1$)    |
  | $\eta_{\text{thermal}}$    | Thermal recovery efficiency              | $\text{dimensionless}$ ($0 \le \eta_{\text{thermal}} \le 1$) |

- Direct integration into electrical power networks (`@modelscript/opendss`) and district heating networks.

# USACE HEC-HMS Watershed Hydrology (`.basin`, `.hms`)

The `@modelscript/hec-hms` package (`languages/hec-hms`) provides native support for the **US Army Corps of Engineers Hydrologic Engineering Center's Hydrologic Modeling System (HEC-HMS)** basin and meteorological models. HEC-HMS is the global industry standard for watershed rainfall-runoff simulation, flood forecasting, urban drainage master planning, and reservoir inflow modeling.

ModelScript compiles HEC-HMS basin decks (`.basin`) into zero-GC WebAssembly DAE linear arenas, verifies topological drainage networks with pre-flight diagnostics (`HMS1001`–`HMS3003`), simulates SCS Dimensionless Unit Hydrograph convolution, routes reaches via the Muskingum method, and directly projects peak flows to **HEC-RAS unsteady flow decks (`.u01`)**.

---

## Supported Hydrologic Model Elements

| Basin Element | Representation                       | Hydrologic & Hydraulic Properties                                                                                              |
| :------------ | :----------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Subbasin**  | Watershed drainage sub-catchment     | Drainage area ($A$), SCS Curve Number ($CN$), initial abstraction ($I_a$), lag time ($T_{\text{lag}}$), impervious percentage. |
| **Reach**     | River / stream channel segment       | Routing method, Muskingum travel time parameter $K$ (hours), weighting factor $X$ ($0.0 \le X \le 0.5$), subreaches.           |
| **Junction**  | Confluence of subbasins/reaches      | Conservation of mass $\sum Q_{\text{in}} = Q_{\text{out}}$, topological routing node.                                          |
| **Reservoir** | Detention pond / storage impoundment | Elevation-storage-outflow discharge rating curves, spillways, gated orifices.                                                  |
| **Sink**      | Watershed outlet / terminal boundary | Terminal drainage point with aggregated hydrograph reporting.                                                                  |

---

## Architecture & Compilation Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    H[".basin / .hms Basin Deck"] --> P["HEC-HMS Parser (parseHmsBasin)"]
    P --> AST["Typed HmsBasinModel AST"]
    AST --> LINT["Topological & Parameter Linter (lintHmsBasin)"]
    AST --> SIM["SCS-CN & Muskingum Solver (simulateSubbasinRunoff / routeMuskingum)"]
    AST --> DAE["Zero-GC DAE Lowering (lowerHmsToDae)"]
    SIM --> RAS["HEC-RAS Boundary Projection (hmsHydrographToHecRasU01)"]

    DAE --> ARENA["Linear Memory DAE Arena (DAEBuilder)"]
    RAS --> U01["HEC-RAS Unsteady Deck (.u01)"]
```

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics (`HMS1001`–`HMS3003`)

The HEC-HMS diagnostic suite validates watershed topology and hydrologic parameters before simulation:

| Code      | Severity  | Description                                                                                |
| :-------- | :-------: | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `HMS1001` | **Error** | Non-positive subbasin drainage area ($A \le 0$).                                           |
| `HMS2001` | **Error** | Element references unknown or non-existent downstream element.                             |
| `HMS2002` | **Error** | Directed cycle detected in watershed drainage connectivity graph.                          |
| `HMS3001` | **Error** | SCS Curve Number outside physically valid bounds ($CN \le 0$ or $CN > 100$).               |
| `HMS3002` | **Error** | Muskingum weighting factor $X$ outside numerical stability range ($X < 0.0$ or $X > 0.5$). |
| `HMS3003` | **Error** | Muskingum travel time parameter $K \le 0$.                                                 |

---

## Command-Line Interface (`msx hec-hms`)

```bash
# Print summary of subbasins, reaches, junctions, and drainage area
msx hec-hms summary CastroValley.basin

# Run pre-flight topological and hydrologic parameter validation
msx hec-hms lint CastroValley.basin

# Simulate 24-hour SCS-CN rainfall runoff event (50mm storm)
msx hec-hms simulate-runoff CastroValley.basin --rain=75.0

# Project simulated peak hydrograph to HEC-RAS unsteady flow boundary (.u01)
msx hec-hms to-ras CastroValley.basin -o boundary.u01

# Lower basin model into WebAssembly DAE arena
msx hec-hms to-dae CastroValley.basin
```

---

## MCP Agent Tool Integration

AI agents connect to `@modelscript/hec-hms` through dedicated MCP tools:

- **`hec_hms_simulate_runoff`**: Evaluates SCS Curve Number excess precipitation, dimensionless unit hydrograph convolution, and Muskingum channel routing directly within agent reasoning workflows.

# OGC WaterML 2.0 Hydrologic Telemetry (`.waterml`, `.wml2`, `.xml`)

The `@modelscript/waterml` package (`languages/waterml`) provides native support for the **Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) WaterML 2.0 / TimeseriesML (OGC 12-031r4 / WMO 1083)** international standard. WaterML 2.0 is the official standard for exchanging water observations, river gauging station telemetry, streamflow timeseries, and water quality observations across agencies such as the USGS (National Water Information System / NWIS), BOM Australia, and Environment Canada.

ModelScript ingests XML/JSON WaterML timeseries, validates sensor metadata and timestamp monotonicity (`WML1001`–`WML3001`), fits non-linear power-law stage-discharge rating curves ($Q = a(h - h_0)^b$), and projects streamflow observations directly into **HEC-RAS unsteady flow (`.u01`)** and **EPANET demand pattern (`[PATTERNS]`)** boundary decks.

---

## Supported WaterML 2.0 Structures

| Structure              | XML Schema Element        | Description                                                                                                                         |
| :--------------------- | :------------------------ | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Observation Series** | `<MeasurementTimeseries>` | Monotonically timestamped hydrologic observations with measurement units, default interpolation, and monitoring point metadata.     |
| **Data Points**        | `<MeasurementTVP>`        | Time-Value Pairs (`<time>`, `<value>`) with observation quality codes and sensor metadata.                                          |
| **Monitoring Point**   | `<MonitoringPoint>`       | Station ID, geographic coordinates (latitude, longitude, elevation), river reach name, datum metadata.                              |
| **Observed Property**  | `<observedProperty>`      | Streamflow discharge (`m³/s` or `cfs`), stage / gauge height (`m` or `ft`), reservoir storage, water temperature, dissolved oxygen. |

---

## Architecture & Compilation Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    W[".waterml / .wml2 XML or JSON"] --> P["WaterML Parser (parseWaterMl)"]
    P --> DOC["Typed WaterMlDocument"]
    DOC --> LINT["Telemetry Integrity Linter (lintWaterMlDocument)"]
    DOC --> FIT["Power-Law Rating Curve Fitter (fitRatingCurve)"]
    DOC --> RAS["HEC-RAS Projection (projectWaterMlToHecRas)"]
    DOC --> EPA["EPANET Pattern Projection (projectWaterMlToEpanet)"]
    DOC --> DAE["Zero-GC DAE Arena Lowering (lowerWaterMlToDae)"]

    DAE --> ARENA["Linear Memory DAE Arena"]
    FIT --> CURVE["Q = a*(h-h0)^b Parameters & RMSE"]
```

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics (`WML1001`–`WML3001`)

The `@modelscript/waterml` linter verifies data quality and monotonicity:

| Code      |  Severity   | Description                                                                    |
| :-------- | :---------: | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WML1001` |  **Error**  | XML syntax error or missing mandatory `<MeasurementTimeseries>` container.     |
| `WML2001` |  **Error**  | Non-monotonic or duplicate observation timestamps detected.                    |
| `WML2002` | **Warning** | Missing physical measurement unit or observed property declaration.            |
| `WML3001` | **Warning** | Physical observation out of bounds (negative discharge or extreme stage jump). |

---

## Command-Line Interface (`msx waterml`)

```bash
# Print summary of timeseries, observation counts, monitoring stations, and units
msx waterml summary usgs_gauge_01646500.xml

# Lint timeseries for timestamp monotonicity and missing units
msx waterml lint usgs_gauge_01646500.xml

# Fit non-linear stage-discharge power-law rating curve Q = a*(h-h0)^b
msx waterml fit-rating usgs_gauge_01646500.xml

# Project streamflow observations to HEC-RAS unsteady flow hydrograph (.u01)
msx waterml to-hec-ras usgs_gauge_01646500.xml -o river_inflow.u01

# Project flow timeseries to EPANET diurnal demand pattern (.inp)
msx waterml to-epanet usgs_gauge_01646500.xml -o network_pattern.inp

# Lower telemetry timeseries into WebAssembly DAE arena
msx waterml to-dae usgs_gauge_01646500.xml
```

---

## MCP Agent Tool Integration

- **`waterml_fit_rating_curve`**: Solves non-linear power-law rating curves from observed hydrologic stage and discharge pairs, reporting equation coefficients ($a, b, h_0$), residual tracking, and RMSE convergence to AI agents.
